The organization has been on guard against internal conspiracies and feuding as they work towards their long-term goals.]

["I've been a hero for more than ten years, now. I'd like to think I know the general beats, how these things work. I'm content to let others take the lead, if they want the responsibilities that come with the role."

Miss Militia, born Hannah, is a key member of the Wardens and a former Protectorate hero. One of the few survivors of a Kurdish village attacked by Turkish soldiers, Hannah triggered during the assault and was later brought to the United States, where she joined the inaugural Wards team.

With dark hair, olive skin, and bottle-glass green eyes, Miss Militia wears stylized military fatigues adorned with an American flag scarf and sash. Her power allows her to manifest various weapons from a green and black blur of energy.

A steady, rational character, Miss Militia is fiercely loyal to the rules and the United States. She prefers not to take on leadership roles, but her unwavering dedication makes her a natural leader. As a Noctis cape, she doesn't need to sleep, instead reliving past events in perfect detail during her rare moments of rest.

Throughout her career, Miss Militia has been a reliable and resourceful hero, forming lasting friendships with her teammates and serving as a mentor to younger capes.]

["I've got a sword and shield, and I'm not afraid to use them! Let's go be heroes and kick some villain butt! Pew pew!"

Mouse Protector, a former member of the inaugural Wards team and later an independent hero, was known for her cheesy puns, dorky behavior, and ability to humiliate villains. As a child, she was loud, outgoing, and irreverent towards authority, often acting silly in inappropriate situations.

During her time with the Wards, Mouse Protector wore a homemade helmet with mouse ears, carrying a sword and shield. Her costume as an adult hero is unknown.

A Grab-Bag Cape, Mouse Protector could mark objects and people, teleporting to them at will. She also possessed minor powers that enhanced her agility, coordination, and stamina. She used these abilities to harass and embarrass her opponents, making their defeats at her hands all the more humiliating.

Tragically, Mouse Protector was captured by the Slaughterhouse Nine and fused with the villain Ravager by Bonesaw, creating the gestalt being Murder Rat. She was later mercy killed by Flashbang during one of Bonesaw's tests.]

["Whoa, Mouse, let's keep it PG! We're supposed to be the good guys, remember?"

Reed, a member of the inaugural Wards team alongside Miss Militia, Chevalier, and Mouse Protector, was a voice of reason among his peers. He often chastised Mouse Protector for her inappropriate behavior, although he himself had to be reminded by Hero not to divulge sensitive information about his teammates.

Wearing a professional black and green costume with a leaf emblem over his heart, Reed's appearance was accompanied by a vague nimbus that warped the surrounding landscape when viewed through Chevalier's secondary power. His actual power remains unknown.

Reed's time with the Wards was marked by the landmark case of Reed v. PRT, in which his parents alleged that he was not given sufficient time or resources to live a full childhood while serving as a Ward. The PRT's loss in this case led to the creation of the Youth Guard.

After leaving the Wards and PRT, Reed's fate is unclear, but his cape name was reused at least twice by the time of the events in Ward, suggesting he had either retired or passed away.]

[The Youth Guard (Y.G.) is an independent organization focused on ensuring the safety and well-being of underage parahumans, particularly those in the Wards program. With approximately 30,000 employees across the United States, including lawyers, outreach workers, and resource officers, the Youth Guard works to protect young capes from physical, mental, and emotional harm.

Through legal action, public sentiment, and collaboration with various agencies, the Youth Guard enforces rules and regulations on the PRT and other teams with underage members. These rules cover aspects such as safety, essential needs, education, and identity, with penalties imposed for violations.

The Youth Guard's involvement with the Wards is more comprehensive, with automatic processes in place for intervention. In contrast, their involvement with non-PRT teams is more limited and often occurs through family court and child welfare services.

The organization's origins can be traced back to the landmark case of Reed v. PRT, which led to the formation of the Youth Guard as a "separate but integrated" entity adjunct to the Wards program. Despite its noble goals, the Youth Guard's scrutiny and actions have been known to contribute to the collapse of some teams, while also providing crucial support to individual young capes in need.]

[The Endbringers are monstrous beings that take turns attacking locations around the globe, causing immense destruction and loss of life. Created by Eidolon to serve as worthy opponents, they have unique abilities and are incredibly durable, with a layered physiology that makes them nearly impossible to kill without exploiting specific vulnerabilities or using powers that ignore conventional durability.

The first three Endbringers were Behemoth, Leviathan, and the Simurgh, followed by Khonsu and the twins, Tohu and Bohu, after Behemoth's death. Each Endbringer has a specific drive that influences their actions, such as Behemoth's drive to break stasis or Leviathan's drive to take away resources.

The Endbringers have had a profound impact on the world, causing demographic shifts, environmental degradation, and the deaths of countless parahumans and civilians. They have also led to the creation of various parahuman organizations and the coordination of the cape community to repel their attacks.

In the original plan, had Eden survived, she would have created "Endbringer Lites" to further the goals of the cycle by inciting conflict between groups. The Endbringers as they exist in the story are significantly more powerful than what Eden had planned, due to Eidolon's influence.]

[Behemoth, the first Endbringer to appear, is a dynakinetic capable of manipulating energy in all forms. He is a physical powerhouse, standing nearly 50 feet tall with gray, leathery skin and cooled magma and obsidian-like crags. His most feared ability is his lack of a Manton limitation within a 32-foot radius, allowing him to burn targets from the inside out.

Behemoth's powers include generating and guiding lightning, projecting radiation, producing powerful shockwaves, unleashing a devastating roar, manipulating fire and heat, and redirecting energy from attacks. He is incredibly durable, able to fight as a skeleton despite losing a significant portion of his body.

Known as the "Herokiller," Behemoth's attacks have resulted in massive casualties, with an average hero death rate of more than one in four. He first appeared in Iran in 1992 and has since attacked various locations worldwide. In his final battle in New Delhi, India, Behemoth was ultimately killed by Scion, becoming the first Endbringer to be defeated.]

[Leviathan, the second Endbringer to appear, is a powerful hydrokinetic capable of manipulating water on a massive scale. He is a 30-foot tall creature with scaly green skin, a disproportionate body, and a prehensile whip-like tail. His face lacks any mouth, nose, or ears, and instead has four asymmetrically placed eyes containing glowing green orbs.

Leviathan's main power is macro-hydrokinesis, which he uses to create tsunamis, extreme water pressure, and erosion. He also has an "after-echo" of water that appears whenever he moves, maintaining the speed and direction of the body part that created it. Additionally, Leviathan possesses super-speed, enhanced strength, and incredible durability due to his Endbringer physiology.

Throughout his attacks on various cities worldwide, such as Oslo, Sydney, Kyushu, Newfoundland, and Brockton Bay, Leviathan has caused immense destruction and loss of life. His actions have led to global consequences, including water crises and the crippling of Japan as a world power.

During Gold Morning, the Simurgh upgraded Leviathan with nano-thorns, making him even more formidable. Despite his power, Leviathan was ultimately killed by Scion during the final battle.]

[The Simurgh, the third and youngest of the original Endbringers, is a powerful precognitive and postcognitive capable of seeing into the past and future of those within her range. She first appeared in Lausanne, Switzerland in 2002, initially seeming benevolent before unleashing a psychic scream that drove the city's residents to violence.

With a 15-foot tall, waif-like human female form and numerous asymmetrical wings, the Simurgh is a cunning planner who uses her abilities to create long-term schemes that lead to tragic outcomes. Her silent scream constantly gathers information, while her active scream can implant mental commands and pull on nearby parahuman abilities, particularly those of Tinkers.

Throughout her appearances, the Simurgh has been responsible for numerous tragedies, including the corruption of Sphere into Mannequin, the quarantining of Madison, Wisconsin, and the creation of the Travelers. She played a key role in the fight against Scion during Gold Morning.

The Simurgh's ultimate goal is revealed to be the creation of a forced parahuman feudalism by merging with Titan Fortuna. Despite her vast power and planning, she is eventually defeated by the combined efforts of Defiant, Dauntless, and other heroes, being flung into Sleeper's storm.]

[Khonsu, the fourth Endbringer to appear, emerged months after Behemoth's death to attack Japan on January 20, 2012. Standing between Leviathan and Behemoth in height, Khonsu has a broad, jet-black body with silver-white accents, resembling a feral Buddha. His unique Endbringer physiology grants him incredible durability, with forcefields between his layers to prevent significant damage from a single attack.

Khonsu's primary ability allows him to create up to three fields of accelerated time, trapping victims inside for what seems like years in mere seconds to outside observers. These fields orbit around him and can be dismissed and resummoned to catch targets. He can also teleport globally, leaving behind massive explosions at his departure point.

During his three-day battle against the world's heroes, Khonsu was eventually driven off by the combined efforts of Cauldron, Moord Nag, and Scion. He later joined forces with the other Endbringers against Scion during Gold Morning but was forced to retreat due to extensive injuries. Following Scion's defeat, Khonsu went dormant.]

[Tohu and Bohu, also known as the Twins, are a pair of Endbringers who first appeared in Bucharest on October 10, 2012. They typically operate together, with Bohu acting as a massive, immobile tower that infests the surrounding area with traps and summons miniature Endbringers, while Tohu serves as Bohu's bodyguard, copying the powers of three nearby parahumans.

Bohu stands at an impressive 1,300 feet tall, with a gaunt, elongated head and a body that widens towards the ground, melding into the landscape. She condenses the city in 24-minute intervals, followed by the creation of barriers, deadfalls, and complex mechanical traps.

Tohu, on the other hand, appears as a feminine figure with three faces, each one twisted to resemble the masks of the parahumans whose powers she has copied. During the Bucharest attack, she was seen using the powers of Eidolon, Legend, and Kazikli Bey simultaneously.

The Twins proved to be formidable opponents, defeating the assembled parahumans in Bucharest and later participating in the assault on Scion during Gold Morning. Their names, Tohu and Bohu, are derived from the Hebrew phrase "Tohu wa-bohu," which translates to "waste and void" or "chaos and desolation."]

[The Slaughterhouse Nine, often simply called the Nine, were a notorious group of supervillains who roamed North America, leaving a trail of death and destruction in their wake. Founded by King, the group was quickly taken over by Jack Slash, who killed King with the aid of Harbinger in 1987.

The Nine were known for their brutality and their practice of recruiting new members through violent tests. They frequently targeted areas recently hit by Endbringers, taking advantage of the chaos. In 2011, they arrived in Brockton Bay, forcing the local heroes and villains to work together to combat them. During this time, they targeted several individuals as potential recruits, including members of the Undersiders.

After escaping Brockton Bay, the Nine continued their rampage, visiting several towns and bolstering their ranks with new members. Bonesaw, one of the Nine, began cloning past and present members, creating an army known as the Slaughterhouse 9000.

The Nine played a crucial role in the events leading up to Gold Morning, with Jack Slash convincing Scion to begin his destruction of humanity. The group's actions and the threat they posed had far-reaching consequences, shaping the lives of many.]

["Get yourself cleaned up, or they will think we are the pathetic sort of monster."

Gabriel Maxberry, known as King, was the original leader of the Slaughterhouse Nine. A broad-shouldered blond man with enhanced strength and endurance, King had the ability to transfer any physical harm he sustained to individuals he had touched within the past 24 hours. This power allowed him to control Gray Boy, a notorious member of the Nine.

As a leader, King ran the Slaughterhouse Nine as a "brute squad," initiating attacks on towns and subjecting individuals to horrific fates. He was a master of psychological torment and enjoyed being in control of dangerous parahumans. King had a habit of raping and murdering young women, and he saw Jack Slash as his "killer-in-training."

In 1987, King was killed by his protégé, Jack Slash, and Harbinger. Years later, during the events of the Slaughterhouse 9000, Bonesaw created clones of King as part of her army. These clones, unaware of the true nature of their original's death, participated in the ensuing chaos. Ultimately, all instances of King were presumed killed during the conflict.]

["You can't shut me out, no matter how hard you try. My voice will always find a way in."

Screamer, one of the founding members of the Slaughterhouse Nine, was a powerful Shaker and Stranger capable of manipulating sound within a mile's radius. She could amplify her voice, alter it to match others, throw it to speak directly into people's ears, or cancel out unwanted sounds. Her abilities also allowed her to hear sounds in any given area, making it nearly impossible to escape her influence.

Known for her sadistic personality, Screamer earned her name from a favored tactic of overloading everyone in her range with a deafening, jarring scream. She could modulate sound to the point that people would hear her voice as if it were their own thoughts, a skill possibly enhanced by working alongside Cherish.

After her death, Screamer was replaced in the Slaughterhouse Nine. However, during the events of the Slaughterhouse 9000, nine clones of Screamer were created by Bonesaw. These clones served as communication specialists for the other cloned members, showcasing the original Screamer's mastery over her power.]

["We asked why he did what he did, setting up the economy, helping. He described it as satisfying, like pressure washing a deck or finishing a puzzle. The outcome is inevitable, it's steady improvement of the world around you."

Kurt Wynn, known as The Number Man and formerly as Harbinger, is a Thinker with the ability to understand and manipulate numbers and probabilities. As a founding member of the Slaughterhouse Nine, he fought alongside Jack Slash before leaving the group and joining Cauldron.

The Number Man purposefully dresses as normal as possible, with a button-down shirt, thin-rimmed glasses, and a clean-shaven appearance. He is known as the "supervillain banker," using his power to manage the finances of major villain groups and influence the global economy.

His power allows him to perceive and manipulate the world through mathematical notations, granting him exceptional combat abilities, architectural understanding, and economic insight. Despite his immense influence, he remains relatively little-known.

The Number Man plays a crucial role in shaping the world, from his early days in the Slaughterhouse Nine to his work with Cauldron and his efforts to stabilize the economy in the aftermath of Gold Morning. He forms a genuine romantic relationship with Citrine and continues to use his power to improve the world, even as he faces the challenges of a post-Scion reality.]
entries.comment: The Number Man, Harbringer, Kurt Wynn

entries.content:
["I'm just a self-hating coward, really. I'd rather ambush my prey than face them head-on."

Breed, born Bradley, was a founding member of the Slaughterhouse Nine known for his ability to create trilobite-like parasites that became more dangerous over time. Despite his fairly normal appearance, Breed's power made him a formidable and terrifying opponent.

As a member of the Nine, Breed acted primarily as an ambusher, using his minions to target vulnerable prey and corpses. His trilobites would burrow into their victims, devouring them from the inside out before molting and seeking new targets. In their final form, these creatures developed natural weapons, including a flesh-melting acid.

Breed was believed to have died when a building he was in collapsed during a heavy ordinance bombardment. However, during the events of the Slaughterhouse 9000, nine clones of Breed were created as part of an effort to bring about the end of the world.

Breed's clones and their minions caused havoc and devastation, participating in various attacks and confrontations. Ultimately, all instances of Breed were seemingly destroyed, save for a single hybrid clone, leaving behind a legacy of horror and destruction.]

["Blood is the key to my power. The more I consume, the stronger I become, like a monstrous Mr. Hyde."

Crimson, one of the founding members of the Slaughterhouse Nine, was a Changer/Brute who gained strength and durability by consuming the blood of his victims. When using his power, Crimson's appearance would transform into a monstrous, muscular form with purple-red, engorged flesh and prominent veins.

Partnered with his lover Winter, Crimson would often rely on her aura to capture victims for him to feed on. Once powered up, he would take to the front lines, drawing fire and protecting Winter as she supported him from a distance. His enhanced strength and agility allowed him to climb buildings, leap across rooftops, and plow through walls with ease.

Despite his fearsome appearance and power, Crimson was not invulnerable. While largely immune to conventional munitions, he could still be harmed by blades and other sharp objects, although he seemed to care little for such injuries.

During the events of the Slaughterhouse 9000, ten clones of Crimson were created by Bonesaw. These clones participated in various battles, with at least one falling to the hero Foil during the Slaughterhouse fight in Los Angeles.]

["Pathetic. Stupid, useless. I thought you’d do something interesting, but you made yourself prey, instead of the predator. If you’re going to be prey, I want you to be my prey."

Nicholas, publicly known as Gray Boy, was a founding member of the Slaughterhouse Nine and one of the most feared villains in the Worm universe. As a prepubescent boy with a monochrome appearance and a private school uniform, Gray Boy's innocent appearance belied his sadistic and unstable personality.

Gray Boy's power allowed him to create stationary time loops, trapping victims in an endless cycle of pain and insanity. His own body was constantly restored to its original state, rendering him effectively immortal. Created by Cauldron and sold to the Slaughterhouse Nine, Gray Boy's mind was deeply affected by his powers, making him dangerously unpredictable.

Under the control of King and later Jack Slash, Gray Boy served as a powerful weapon for the Nine, indiscriminately using his powers to torture and terrorize. Even after his death at the hands of Glaistig Uaine, his legacy as one of the most terrifying villains persisted.

During the events of the Slaughterhouse 9000, a clone of Gray Boy created by Bonesaw proved to be just as sadistic and powerful as the original, playing a crucial role in Jack Slash's endgame before being killed by Foil.]

["You can't escape my poison, no matter how hard you try. It'll seep into your mind, your body, until there's nothing left but a husk."

Nyx, a Case 53 and founding member of the Slaughterhouse Nine, was a terrifying villain known for her ability to release poisonous gas from the vents on her pale red skin. With overlarge black eyes and a small Cauldron emblem tattooed on her face like a beauty mark, Nyx's appearance was as unsettling as her powers.

Nyx and her twin sister, Nix, both took Cauldron vials, but while Nix gained viable powers, Nyx became a "monstrous cape" and was released into the world as another Case 53. As a member of the Slaughterhouse Nine, Nyx honed her abilities, learning to shape her poisonous gas into solid forms that moved at her will, capable of knocking out or even causing permanent brain damage and organ failure to those who inhaled it.

During the events of the Slaughterhouse 9000, several clones of Nyx were created by Bonesaw, showcasing the original's terrifying skill with her power. These clones participated in various battles, with some falling to heroes like Crucible and Contessa, while others used their illusions to deceive and disguise members of the Nine.]

[Case 53s, also known as Deviants or the Branded, are a group of parahumans characterized by their monstrous or bizarre physical appearances and a shared set of circumstances surrounding their origins. First discovered in urban areas across the world, Case 53s exhibit retrograde amnesia, with their earliest memories being waking up in a strange city. Each bears a distinctive tattoo resembling the Greek letter Omega or a stylized "C" somewhere on their body.

In reality, Case 53s are the results of Cauldron's experiments to artificially create parahumans. Subjected to doses of formula, these individuals were often taken from near-death situations, their injuries healed or compensated for by their newfound powers. Those who survived the process with severe physical mutations were dubbed "deviations." Cauldron erased their memories using the Slug to maintain secrecy and branded them with their symbol before releasing them into the world.

Less than a hundred Case 53s were released onto Earth Bet, with the majority kept as prisoners or brainwashed operatives within Cauldron's compound. These parahumans were strategically placed to provoke aversive reactions in Scion and serve as distractions, allowing Cauldron to pursue their goals with less interference.]

["Reality is what I make it. Your mind, your fears, your darkest nightmares - they're all just clay for me to mold."

Psychosoma, born Rafael, was a founding member of the Slaughterhouse Nine known for his ability to trap people in semi-real illusions of horrifying monsters. A tall, bald man with a pencil-thin mustache, beard, and spidery fingers, Psychosoma's narrow frame belied the power of his mind.

As a member of the Nine, Psychosoma used his power to sedate and torment his victims, wrapping them in brittle illusions of monsters with sharp claws, strong jaws, and the ability to crawl up walls. His high ratings as a Stranger and Master reflected the danger he posed to civilian populations.

During the events of the Slaughterhouse 9000, ten clones of Psychosoma were created by Bonesaw. These clones participated in various battles, with some engaging the hero Golem and others falling to the combined efforts of the Dragon's Teeth, Protectorate, and Wards.

Despite his eventual death, Psychosoma's legacy as one of the original members of the Slaughterhouse Nine and the terror he inflicted with his mind-bending powers remains a dark chapter in the history of Earth Bet.]

["I've come to be a fan of small towns. Fewer people to get in my way, more people who know each other. Easier to get the real fun started."

Jacob Black, better known as Jack Slash, is the charismatic and sadistic leader of the Slaughterhouse Nine. With an attractive face, pale blue eyes, and a neatly trimmed goatee, Jack's appearance belies his cruel and manipulative nature.

Jack's primary power allows him to extend the cutting edge of any handheld blade, granting him effectively infinite range. However, his true strength lies in his secondary power, a subtle manipulation of the shard network that turns parahumans into unwitting pawns in his schemes.

Under Jack's leadership, the Slaughterhouse Nine became synonymous with terror, leaving a trail of death and destruction across the United States. His love of theatrics and his ability to exploit the weaknesses of both heroes and villains made him a formidable opponent.

Despite his grand ambitions and his role in setting the end of the world in motion, Jack's core remained shallow, his charisma a product of his powers rather than his personality. In the end, it was his reliance on this power that proved to be his undoing, as a non-parahuman was able to catch him off guard and set the stage for his ultimate defeat.]

["I'm a good girl, I am! I do what Uncle Jack and Sibby tell me, and I make the most amazing art. You'll see, once I've made you better!"

Riley Grace Davis, better known as Bonesaw, was a member of the Slaughterhouse Nine and one of the most terrifying Tinkers. With blonde hair in perfect ringlets, mismatched blue and green eyes, and a blood-splattered apron over her dress, Bonesaw's innocent appearance belied her monstrous acts.

Bonesaw triggered at age six after being forced by the Nine to repeatedly operate on her dying family. Her power gave her unparalleled expertise in biological and anatomical modification, which she used to create grotesque "art" from her victims and to augment her teammates into more durable killing machines.

Childish and depraved, Bonesaw craved the approval of her "family," particularly Jack Slash and Siberian. She took delight in torture and murder, justifying her actions as the pursuit of art. However, beneath her persona lay the broken remnants of Riley, the scared little girl who once loved her family.

During Gold Morning, Bonesaw began to doubt her allegiance to Jack and to distinguish between herself and her passenger. She joined the heroes in the fight against Scion, though her true path to redemption would be a long and difficult one.]

["Being wild. Being free. Truly free. It's exhilarating."

The Siberian, one of the most terrifying members of the Slaughterhouse Nine, was an unstoppable force and an immovable object. With her black and white striped skin, long hair, and piercing yellow eyes, the Siberian's naked form was a sight that struck fear into the hearts of heroes and villains alike.

Created by the reclusive parahuman Dr. William Manton, the Siberian was a projection that could bestow her invulnerability upon anything she touched. She was immune to all physical forces and most parahuman powers, able to tear through even the toughest defenses with ease.

The Siberian's personality was as wild and untamed as her appearance suggested. She relished the destruction she caused and the fear she instilled in others. Despite her feral nature, she had a maternal bond with Bonesaw and an unexpected insight into the minds of those around her.

Throughout her years with the Slaughterhouse Nine, the Siberian fought against the Triumvirate and other powerful heroes, leaving a trail of carnage in her wake. It was only through the discovery of her true nature as a projection and the elimination of her master that the Siberian was finally defeated, though her legacy as one of the most terrifying villains.]

["It was all so pointless, wasn't it? We thought we could make a difference, but in the end, the world just keeps on turning, no matter how hard we try."

Alan Gramme, once known as the heroic Tinker Sphere, is now the monstrous Mannequin of the Slaughterhouse Nine. Driven to despair by the loss of his family and the apparent futility of his efforts to better the world, Mannequin now seeks to destroy those who would follow in his former footsteps.

Encased in a modular, white, eggshell-smooth carapace, Mannequin stands an imposing nine feet tall. His body is a testament to his Tinker abilities, a self-contained life support system bristling with weapons and tools. Each segment of his form is flexible and capable of independent movement, making him a unpredictable and relentless foe.

As a member of the Nine, Mannequin targets rogues, idealistic Tinkers, and those who seek to use their powers for good. His mechanical nature and unique physiology make him one of the group's longest-surviving members, able to repair and reconfigure himself after even the most devastating injuries.

Despite his monstrous appearance and actions, there are hints of the man he once was, a fact that Jack Slash ruthlessly exploits to keep him in line. Yet Mannequin remains a implacable foe, his idealism forever twisted into a dark reflection of itself.]

["You want to hurt me? Good fucking luck. Give it your best shot, and watch me come back stronger than ever. That's what I live for."

Ned, better known as Crawler, is a monstrous member of the Slaughterhouse Nine whose adaptive regeneration allows him to survive almost any attack and become resistant to similar damage in the future. Originally a narrow-shouldered man of average height, Crawler's masochistic desire to be injured has transformed him into a hulking, multi-limbed beast covered in iridescent black armor plates, scales, and bristling spines.

Driven by an insatiable hunger for pain and the thrill of overcoming new threats, Crawler eagerly throws himself into the path of danger. He revels in his role as a monster, taunting and torturing his victims with sadistic glee. His ultimate goal is to one day face an opponent capable of truly testing his limits, even if it means his own destruction.

As a member of the Nine, Crawler's resilience and relentless pursuit of adversity make him one of the group's most fearsome assets. His regeneration is so potent that only attacks capable of destroying his core or obliterating him entirely can bypass his adaptive defenses, a weakness that would eventually spell his doom during the Nine's rampage through Brockton Bay.]

["I am not some common thug or simple-minded brute. I am an artist, and the world is my canvas. The Nine understand this, and that is why I belong with them."

Shatterbird, a powerful silica kinetic and member of the Slaughterhouse Nine, sees herself as a scholar and an artist, using her ability to control glass and sand to create devastating "masterpieces" of destruction. Born in the United Arab Emirates and later dosed with a Cauldron formula, Shatterbird's power manifested violently, killing thousands and setting her on the path to becoming one of the Nine's most notorious members.

With her glass helmet, beaked mask, and flowing garment of colored shards, Shatterbird cuts a striking figure. Her pride and need for validation drive her to seek power and respect from both her teammates and her victims. She revels in the psychological impact of her attacks, which often involve causing every piece of glass in a city to explode as a herald of the Nine's arrival.

As the Nine's primary recruiter, Shatterbird has an eye for potential new members who can thrive among the group's monstrous ranks. However, her pride and control-freak tendencies often put her at odds with others, particularly those who threaten her status or reputation. Ultimately, it was this very pride that led to her downfall during the battle against Echidna in Brockton Bay.]

["Besides, the freedom to do what I wanted and go where I wished kind of lost its appeal when the boredom set in. I would've done it even if my big brothers weren't coming for me, but I joined the Nine. Well. That was dumb."

Cherie Vasil, better known as Cherish, is the wayward daughter of the notorious villain Heartbreaker and the eldest sister of Regent. Born into a family of emotionally stunted manipulators, Cherish's ability to sense and control emotions led her down a dark path of exploitation and murder.

A slim, attractive young woman with dark hair and a distinctive red streak, Cherish's appearance belies her sociopathic tendencies. She revels in using her power to twist others' emotions, seeing them as little more than playthings for her amusement.

Desperate to escape her father's control, Cherish fled her family and nominated herself to join the Slaughterhouse Nine. Despite enduring the group's brutal initiation tests, which left her with hideous tattoos and scars, Cherish's attempts to subvert and control the Nine were ultimately discovered, leading to her downfall.

As punishment for her betrayal, Bonesaw modified Cherish's powers to force her to sense only negative emotions and imprisoned her in a life-sustaining container at the bottom of the bay. Trapped in an endless cycle of despair and unable to die, Cherish serves as a testament to the consequences of crossing the Slaughterhouse Nine.]

["It's not like I want to do these things, you know? But when the fire starts, it's like… it's like I can't help myself. The more I use my power, the harder it is to stop."

Mimi, better known as Burnscar, is a tragic figure whose pyrokinetic abilities come at the cost of her mental stability. A former patient at the Parahuman Asylum, Mimi's treasured memories of her friendship with Labyrinth are tainted by the reality that the guards used Elle as a means to control her.

With badly cut dark brown hair, green eyes, and cigarette burns marring her pale skin from her eyes to her jaw, Burnscar's appearance reflects the pain and instability that plague her. Her voice, devoid of emotion, hints at the emptiness within.

As a member of the Slaughterhouse Nine, Burnscar's power feeds into a vicious cycle: the more she uses it, the more detached and reckless she becomes, leading her to use it even more. She finds solace in the company of her fellow monsters, but in her lucid moments, the guilt of her actions threatens to consume her.

Burnscar's ultimate fate, her head crushed by Grue's manifestation of Siberian's power, serves as a grim reminder of the destructive path she walked and the price she paid for her powers.]

[Hack Job, the nightmarish fusion of Hatchet Face and Oni Lee, is a testament to Bonesaw's twisted genius and disregard for human life. Created after the deaths of the two villains, Hack Job combines Hatchet Face's brute strength and power nullification with Oni Lee's clone teleportation, making him a formidable and terrifying opponent.

With Hatchet Face's tall, muscular, and heavily scarred frame serving as the main body, Oni Lee's remains are grotesquely grafted onto his back and shoulders, a tumor-like growth with a face gasping for air. The patchwork of flesh and mechanical components holding the two together only adds to the horror of this abomination.

While Hatchet Face's lobotomized state renders him little more than a mindless puppet under Bonesaw's control, Oni Lee's consciousness remains trapped within, fully aware of his situation but unable to influence their shared body.

As Bonesaw's bodyguard and enforcer, Hack Job's presence strikes fear into the hearts of her victims, his very existence a grim reminder of the Slaughterhouse Nine's capacity for cruelty and depravity. Though ultimately destroyed by Sundancer, the legacy of Hack Job undoubtedly influenced Bonesaw's future creations, a testament to the depths of her madness and the lengths she will go to in her pursuit of the perfect monster.]

[Pagoda, the monstrous fusion of two regenerators, Carnal and Prophet, stands as a testament to Bonesaw's twisted creativity and disregard for human life. This centaur-like abomination, with the muscular, gorilla-like lower body of Carnal and the thin, greasy-haired upper body of Prophet, is a nightmarish vision of mismatched flesh and unnatural regeneration.

Carnal, once a prospective member of the Slaughterhouse Nine, failed his tests and fell victim to Bonesaw's experiments. Prophet, a delusional regenerator convinced of his divine status, met a similar fate. Together, they form the basis of Pagoda, a being capable of healing from almost any injury at an astonishing rate.

Stripped of their individuality and free will, Pagoda is little more than a puppet, controlled by the metal framework implanted within his body. His brain, warped by Bonesaw's modifications, no longer processes pain properly, and his dual nature grants him immunity to most Master effects.

As a failsafe, Bonesaw has equipped Pagoda with a device that can reverse his regeneration, ensuring his loyalty through the threat of an agonizing death. In the end, Pagoda serves as a grim reminder of the depths of Bonesaw's cruelty and the fate that awaits those who cross the Slaughterhouse Nine.]

[Quarantine Sites are designated areas affected by ongoing S-class or other problematic parahuman events that require constant monitoring and containment by the PRT. These sites, ranging from abandoned cities to sealed-off zones, serve as a grim reminder of the devastating impact that parahumans can have on the world.

Some notable Quarantine Sites include Ellisburg, New York, where the monstrous creations of the parahuman Nilbog roam free; Madison, Wisconsin, a city forever changed by the Simurgh's influence; and Eagleton, Tennessee, where the relentless Machine Army threatens to overrun the region.

The PRT often assigns problematic capes to Quarantine Site duty as a form of punishment or as a way to channel their destructive tendencies into a more beneficial role. These capes, alongside specialized patrols and guards, work to maintain the fragile containment of these sites, ensuring that the horrors within do not spread to the rest of the world.

As a testament to the ever-present danger posed by parahumans, Quarantine Sites serve as a chilling reminder of the constant vigilance required to maintain the delicate balance between the powered and the powerless.]

["I am the Goblin King, the lord of my domain! You dare enter my kingdom, my Garden of Eden, without invitation? Begone, or face the wrath of my children!"

Jamie Rinke, once a lonely accountant, now rules the quarantined city of Ellisburg as the monstrous Nilbog. Triggered by the trauma of losing his job and facing homelessness, Rinke's power allows him to create customized minions from living matter, earning him an S-Class threat rating.

With a potbellied, hunchbacked appearance and a patchwork costume of jarring patterns, Nilbog presents a disturbing visage. His cloth crown and perpetually leering mask hide a childish perception of himself as a god, a result of years of isolation among his sycophantic creations.

Nilbog's ability to create self-replicating monsters with their own unique powers makes him a formidable foe, capable of wiping out entire cities if left unchecked. Despite his megalomaniac tendencies and fairy-tale mentality, his unpredictability and the sheer scope of his power cement his status as one of the most dangerous parahumans in the Worm universe.

Contained within Ellisburg, Nilbog remains a constant threat, his very existence serving as a reminder of the devastating potential of unchecked parahuman abilities and the importance of the PRT's containment efforts.]

["Do not wake the Evil while it is quiet."

Sleeper, an enigmatic S-Class threat, is a name whispered in fear by even the most powerful parahumans. Little is known about this dormant villain, who spends most of his time in the remote regions of Russia, but his reputation alone is enough to inspire terror.

When roused, Sleeper's power manifests as a mesmerizing storm of crackling, boiling rainbow shimmers that engulfs vast areas, blocking communications and trapping anyone caught within. Even the mighty Simurgh, when flung into Sleeper's storm, was rendered helpless and prone, a testament to the sheer potency of his abilities.

Despite his immense power, Sleeper remains largely inactive, content to sit and read aloud to himself in solitude. However, when provoked or motivated, he becomes an unstoppable force, requiring the intervention of the world's most powerful heroes to deter him from emerging.

As an S-Class threat on par with the Endbringers and the Slaughterhouse Nine, Sleeper serves as a chilling reminder of the untold horrors lurking in the shadows of the Worm universe, a sleeping giant whose true potential remains a mystery even to those who dedicate their lives to understanding and containing the world's most dangerous parahumans.]

["You killed him! You killed Coil! He was going to save me, and you killed him! I'll make you pay for what you've done, I swear it!"

Noelle Meinhardt, a member of the Travelers from Earth Aleph, was a young woman with straight brown hair who struggled with anorexia. She was the former leader and tactical mastermind of her gaming group, known for her clever strategies and instinctive decision-making.

After being transported to Earth Bet during the Simurgh's attack on Madison, Noelle and her boyfriend, Francis Krouse, each took half a dose of a Cauldron formula. This triggered her transformation into the monstrous Echidna, with the ability to create twisted clones of anyone she touched. From the waist up, she appears as her former self, but below is a grotesque mass of flesh, limbs, and animal parts.

Echidna's mind is as fractured as her body, with her aggressive and destructive impulses constantly at war with her fading humanity. Her only anchor is her boyfriend, Trickster, whose presence helps keep her volatile emotions in check.

With the ability to create twisted clones of anyone she touches, Echidna is a walking nightmare, capable of producing an army of powerful, psychotic doppelgangers. Her immense strength, regenerative powers, and tactical cunning make her a threat on par with the Endbringers.

Driven by a desperate desire to be cured and a burning hatred for those she believes have wronged her, Echidna rampages across Brockton Bay, leaving a trail of destruction and horror in her wake. In the end, it falls to her former friend, Sundancer, to make the heartbreaking decision to end Echidna's suffering, incinerating her and the capes trapped within her monstrous form.]

["I am the Ash Beast, a force of nature, a living inferno. My existence is a constant cycle of destruction and rebirth, a testament to the raw power of the shard within me."

The Ash Beast, a walking calamity, is an S-Class threat that roams the African continent, leaving a trail of devastation in his wake. Believed to have triggered in Matruh, Egypt, or possibly the result of a Cauldron vial, the Ash Beast is a being consumed by his own power.

Appearing as a humanoid figure at the center of an unending explosion, the Ash Beast's form shifts and changes within the flames, manifesting wings or claws as he rampages across the landscape. His power, a constant conversion of matter to energy and back again, grants him regenerative abilities and a destructive capacity rivaling that of the Endbringers.

Yet, for all his might, the Ash Beast is a tragic figure, his humanity subsumed by the shard that controls him. His slow, predictable path allows settlements to evacuate before his arrival, a small mercy in the face of an unstoppable force.

In the end, it took the intervention of Khepri and her army of controlled capes to bring the Ash Beast to bear against Scion, a final act of destruction before his ultimate erasure at the hands of the golden man.]

["I'm not trying to end the world, man. I just want to create something beautiful, something that'll make people stop and think. Is that so wrong?"

Rey Andino, better known as the villain Blasto, is a "wet" Tinker who specializes in creating living organisms and hybrids. Born into a struggling family, Rey's gift for science and medicine alienated him from his loved ones and peers alike. Triggered by the crumbling of both his personal and professional lives, he fully embraced his powers and the life of a villain.

With frizzy brown hair and a laid-back demeanor, Blasto is an anti-establishment figure who seeks to push the boundaries of his art. His creations, ranging from plant-animal hybrids to pseudo-Endbringers, are a testament to his skill and ambition.

Despite his potential for destruction, Blasto is content to maintain his territory in Boston, feuding with rivals like Accord and the Slaughterhouse Nine. His on-again, off-again relationship with Rotten Apple provides a glimpse into his desire for normalcy and appreciation.

Ultimately, Blasto's hubris proves to be his undoing. Captured and tortured by the Slaughterhouse Nine, he meets a grim end, leaving behind a legacy of chaos and untapped potential in the world of Earth Bet.]

["Every time you think of me or mention me, I will be there. I will know where you are and see what you are doing. I will take stock and I will make my judgments."

Christine Mathers, better known as Mama Mathers, is the matriarch of the Mathers clan within the Fallen. Abandoned by her family due to a teen pregnancy, she was saved by Cauldron and granted powers that allow her to control others without becoming a slave herself.

Emaciated and frail in appearance, with bleached, frayed hair, Mama Mathers belies her true power and influence. Her ability to infect the senses of anyone who perceives her, creating a network of surveillance and control, makes her a formidable and terrifying adversary.

A true believer in the Fallen's ideology, Mama Mathers rules her family with an iron fist, demanding absolute devotion and ruthlessly punishing those who disappoint her. Her power allows her to elude authorities and build entire communities of followers, cementing her status as a potential S-Class threat.

Despite her fragile appearance, Mama Mathers is a cunning and subtle player in Earth Bet, using her powers to manipulate and control those around her while always prioritizing her own safety and the success of the Fallen.]

[The Battle against Echidna, which took place on June 20, 2011, was a pivotal conflict in Brockton Bay between the monstrous Echidna and the combined forces of the Protectorate, the Undersiders, and various other cape groups. Echidna, formerly known as Noelle Meinhardt of the Travelers, had escaped from Coil's base and begun a rampage, creating twisted clones of the capes she absorbed.

The battle escalated from an A-Class to an S-Class threat, drawing in the Triumvirate and other powerful capes. Despite heavy casualties, including the death of Myrddin and several other heroes, Echidna was eventually killed by her former teammate, Sundancer.

The aftermath of the battle had far-reaching consequences, as the existence of Cauldron and their connection to the Triumvirate was revealed by an Eidolon clone. This revelation led to the formation of the Irregulars, a group of disgruntled Case 53s, and sowed discord within the Protectorate. The battle also resulted in the opening of a portal to Earth Gimel in Brockton Bay, setting the stage for future developments.]

[The Slaughterhouse Nine-Thousand, a major conflict that took place on June 19, 2013, marked the revival of the notorious Slaughterhouse Nine. After obtaining advanced technology from Toybox, the remaining members of the Nine, led by Jack Slash and Bonesaw, spent two years in a pocket dimension, creating clones of past and present members.

With nearly 300 clones, the Nine-Thousand launched simultaneous attacks across the United States, targeting cities such as Killington, Schenectady, and Ellisburg. The Protectorate, along with groups like the Undersiders and the Thanda, fought back against the Nine's onslaught.

The final battle took place in Los Angeles, where most of the remaining members of the Nine were defeated. However, Jack Slash, trapped by Weaver, managed to trigger Gold Morning by communicating with Scion.

The Slaughterhouse Nine-Thousand showcased the terrifying potential of Bonesaw's cloning technology and the sheer chaos the Nine could unleash. Although the clones were generally less experienced and less connected to their powers than the originals, their coordinated attacks and psychological enhancements made them a formidable threat. The aftermath of the event led directly to the beginning of the end, as Jack Slash's machinations set the stage for Scion's rampage.]

[The Three Blasphemies, a group of enigmatic and powerful supervillains, have been a constant threat to the political landscape of Europe. Composed of three alabaster-skinned women wearing masks depicting various expressions, the Blasphemies are the result of multiple Tinkers simultaneously and independently creating nearly identical beings, possibly as part of an unknown plan by the Shards.

With abilities that allow them to survive against even the most formidable opponents, such as Eidolon, and the power to reconstitute themselves as long as one member remains, the Blasphemies have proven to be a persistent and dangerous force. Their actions, including the assassination of the Dutch King and Queen, have had far-reaching consequences and have been speculated to be in service of an unknown European nation.

During Gold Morning, the Blasphemies participated in a Cauldron meeting to discuss the threat of Scion, showcasing their importance in the grand scheme of the Worm universe. Even Khepri, with her vast powers of control, was unable to subjugate these inhuman beings.]

[Francis Krouse, better known as Trickster, is the controversial leader of the Travelers. Transferred to Earth Bet by the Simurgh and granted powers through a Cauldron vial, Trickster's life has been a series of desperate attempts to save his girlfriend, Noelle, from the monstrous effects of her own power.

With light brown skin, long dark hair, and a piercing gaze, Trickster cuts a striking figure in his black costume, red mask, and top hat. His power allows him to swap the locations of two objects with similar mass, a versatile ability he employs with cunning and ruthlessness.

Trickster's abrasive personality and lack of empathy often put him at odds with his teammates and allies. His unwavering devotion to Noelle drives him to make questionable decisions, ultimately leading to his downfall and capture by the Protectorate.]

[WEDGDG, commonly known as Watchdog, is a PRT sub-organization tasked with preventing economic and political disruption caused by parahumans. Employing both powered and unpowered individuals, Watchdog uses think tanks of Thinkers to analyze vast amounts of data, identifying anomalies and potential threats.

Watchdog's scope of operations covers a wide range, from the political sphere and financial markets to international crime and parahuman science. The organization also serves as an internal affairs division for the PRT, launching investigations and providing consultation for handling parahuman-related issues.

Notable members of Watchdog include the villainous Accord, who once siphoned funds from the organization before turning to a life of crime, and the precognitive Case 53 Hunch, who remained with the PRT despite the revelations of the Echidna incident.

Following the Gold Morning event, Watchdog was dissolved as an organization. However, its legacy as a crucial oversight committee within the PRT remains a significant part of history, dedicated to maintaining stability in the face of parahuman influence.]

["I like order, Trickster. Order means everything has its place. And everyone has their place. Your subordinate's place was not here. […] Rest assured, it's better to eliminate this disordered element before it does too much damage."

Accord, the mastermind behind the Ambassadors, is a meticulous and ruthless Thinker whose intelligence scales with the complexity of the problems he faces. Once a member of the PRT's WEDGDG, Accord's frustration with the world's disinterest in his elaborate plans led him down the path of villainy.

Standing barely over five feet tall, Accord dresses in impeccable white suits and an ornate wood-and-silver mask, his appearance reflecting his obsession with order and perfection. His power has left him hypersensitive to disorder, driving him to homicidal rage over even the slightest infractions.

Despite his volatile temperament, Accord is a brilliant strategist and problem-solver, capable of devising intricate plans for everything from ending world hunger to eliminating his enemies. He demands absolute obedience and perfection from his subordinates, and his wrath is legendary among those who have crossed him.

Accord's legacy is one of grand ambitions and ruthless methods, a testament to the lengths he would go to impose his vision of order upon a chaotic world. Though his life was cut short by a former enemy, his meticulous plans continued to shape the world long after his demise.]

[The Ambassadors are a group of powerful parahumans who serve as the personal assistants and secretaries of the mastermind Thinker, Accord. Handpicked by Accord for their potential and subjected to rigorous testing, the Ambassadors are given top-tier Cauldron vials to enhance their abilities and ensure their loyalty to Accord's grand plans for the betterment of humanity.

Known for their colorful, tailored, and thematic costumes, the Ambassadors are a formidable force in the field, especially when under Accord's direct command. Each member is considered a heavy hitter in their own right, with powers ranging from reality manipulation to regeneration auras and intelligence stealing.

Despite suffering losses during the Slaughterhouse Nine's attack on Boston, the Ambassadors persevered and later joined the Undersiders in Brockton Bay. Following Accord's death, Citrine, his most trusted Ambassador, took over leadership of the group, ensuring that Accord's legacy and vision would continue to shape the world even in his absence.]

["When you decide the outcome first and results are virtually assured, then it's inevitable that it's reduced to these kinds of decisions. Always maddeningly hard ones, both good, both bad. This is how Cauldron operates."

Cauldron, a secret organization operating across multiple dimensions, was formed by Doctor Mother and Contessa with the ultimate goal of defeating Scion and preventing the end of humanity. By harvesting and refining parts of the dead Entity Eden, they created vials that granted powers to those who consumed them, albeit with unpredictable results and side effects.

Cauldron's modus operandi involved selling these vials to carefully selected clients, often manipulating them into debt or servitude. They also engaged in social engineering, setting up powerful parahuman groups worldwide to maintain stability and cultivate a culture welcoming to parahumans. The organization was led by Doctor Mother, with Contessa and others providing advice and support.

Notable members included the Triumvirate (Alexandria, Eidolon, and Legend), as well as the Number Man, William Manton, and various Case 53s. Despite their morally questionable methods, Cauldron played a crucial role in shaping the world of parahumans, all in preparation for the inevitable confrontation with Scion. However, their actions also led to the creation of dangerous threats like the Siberian and the revelation of their existence during the Echidna incident.]

["You made sacrifices, you made sacrifices on the behalf of others, and you made the hard calls, but it was all for something greater. I bet you think you won't have any regrets at the end."

"It's been some time since I lost sleep because of a heavy conscience."

Doctor Mother, the enigmatic leader of Cauldron, is an ordinary human from the Ivory Coast who found herself stranded in another dimension during Eden's collision with Earth. Together with Contessa, she killed the Entity and formed Cauldron to save humanity from Scion.

A dark-skinned woman with long hair and a doctor's attire, Doctor Mother is emotionally detached and well-spoken, her English tinged with a French accent. She kept the nature of their foe secret while overseeing the distribution of superpowers through Cauldron's vials, as well as the kidnapping and testing of civilians who became Case 53s.

Cold and calculating, Doctor Mother made countless sacrifices and hard decisions in the name of the greater good. During Gold Morning, as Scion attacked Cauldron's headquarters, she attempted to gain powers by drinking a vial, but was accidentally killed by Sveta before she could do so, her morally gray legacy forever shaping the world of parahumans.]

["Everything was easy now. It was disorienting."

Contessa, a founding member of Cauldron, is one of the most powerful parahumans in existence. Born as Fortuna on an alternate Earth, she gained her powers during Eden's crash-landing and used them to kill the Entity with the help of Doctor Mother.

Contessa is a pale-skinned woman with black, wavy-to-curly hair worn slightly longer than shoulder length. She dresses in a tailored black suit with a white dress shirt, black tie, and fedora.

Her power, known as "Path to Victory," allows her to see the steps needed to achieve almost any goal and execute them perfectly. Cold and calculating, Contessa serves as Doctor Mother's bodyguard and right-hand woman in Cauldron. She is feared by those who know of her existence, with one Protectorate cape classifying her as "Thinker. Don't worry about the number. Just run."

Despite her power's vast applications, Contessa does have some limitations and blind spots, including Eidolon, the Endbringers, Scion, and trigger events. Nevertheless, her ability to path almost any goal makes her an invaluable asset to Cauldron and a terrifying force on Earth Bet.]

[Balminder, known publicly as "The Dealer," is a mysterious figure who sells superpowers through Cauldron vials. A middle-aged Indian man with long hair and a beard, Balminder is an expert on parahumans and one of the few individuals who cannot be found by Cauldron's Clairvoyant.

Balminder's background is largely unknown, but he is believed to have escaped from Cauldron, similar to Subject 777. He carries many Cauldron vials with him and has been investigated by the PRT, who opened a case file on him.

Balminder came to the attention of Faultline while she was investigating her subordinate Gregor's origins. One of Balminder's clients was murdered by two unnamed capes shortly after making a blog post about their transaction with him.

As a rogue parahuman expert and power broker, Balminder plays a small but intriguing role in Earth Bet, providing a glimpse into the shadowy world of Cauldron and the distribution of powers outside of the organization's direct control.]

["I can't… too much to look at. So many worlds at once."

"I'm… I'm pretty scared."

Doormaker, one of Cauldron's earliest successful vial recipients, is a pale-skinned, plain-looking, and thin young man with a blank and unfocused gaze. His power allows him to create portals between different locations and dimensions, making him a crucial asset to Cauldron's operations.

Almost always accompanied by the Clairvoyant, Doormaker's abilities come at a cost. Perceiving too many worlds at once has left him functionally blind and deaf, likely due to overexposure to the Clairvoyant's power. Despite this, he remains a vital part of Cauldron, transporting members wherever they need to go and acting as a gatekeeper to their facilities.

During Gold Morning, Khepri exploited Doormaker's powers to bring the fight to Scion, pushing him to his limits. When his power eventually ran dry, Khepri released him, and Doormaker was able to communicate his experiences before being killed by Glaistig Uaine, who then claimed his power for herself.]

["He'd been too young a subject when he'd taken the formula, his brain too malleable for the required changes, too slow to form natural immunities and defenses. Even now as he was reaching his late teens, the boy's mind had never developed beyond the mental age of eight, and his eyes remained like twin ashtrays."

The Clairvoyant, a pale young man in his late teens, is a member of Cauldron and Doormaker's constant companion. His eyes, described as "twin ashtrays" or "flat expanses of skin," burned out when he triggered after taking a Cauldron potion at too young an age, leaving his mental development stunted at around eight years old.

The Clairvoyant's power allows him to view wide areas, multiple things at once, and even other universes. He can grant visions of entire alternate Earths to those he touches, but breaking contact renders the recipient unconscious and weakened for a week. His abilities are crucial to Cauldron's operations, as Doormaker uses them to determine where to open, close, or maintain portals.

During Gold Morning, the Clairvoyant was used by Khepri in the fight against Scion. Despite his immense power, the Clairvoyant remains a tragic figure, his potential forever limited by the circumstances of his trigger event.]

["I could sense her more than before, a disturbance, agitated. She was the one that had been enforcing the peace, keeping people contained in cells without doors. Now… either Mantellum or the strange case fifty-threes were keeping her at bay, preventing her from seeing to her duties."

The Custodian, an ex-member of the Cauldron staff, is a parahuman made of air, invisible and almost completely incorporeal. Bound to the Cauldron complex, she is essentially omnipresent, able to manifest her powers by shifting her focus and creating temporary duplicates of herself.

Despite the horrendous wrong done to her, the Custodian voluntarily took on a role in Cauldron, serving as a one-woman maintenance staff and a viable counter and containment measure for the numerous Deviant cases housed within the facility. Her power is limited mostly by her attention span or cramped environments.

The Custodian considers herself duty-bound to protect the Cauldron Compound and act as a warden for the people there. Although unable to communicate with most people, she develops ways to give herself a "voice" with individuals like The Number Man, Satyrical, and Taylor. During Gold Morning, the Custodian assisted both Taylor's assault team and Vegas Dark in finding Doctor Mother, showcasing her unwavering commitment to her role within Cauldron.]

["Oh, I did mention I wouldn't be on the team in the future. Not because of any injuries, mind you. I'm facing a stay in prison. My captain and I were the only ones left. He grabbed the rope ladder first, but he didn't climb fast enough. I shot him."

Coil, real name Thomas Calvert, is a supervillain operating in Brockton Bay. With a power that seemingly allows him to split timelines and choose the most favorable outcome, Coil is a meticulous and paranoid planner, always ensuring his own security and protection.

As Coil, he wears a skintight black bodysuit with a white snake curling around it. In his civilian identity, he is a tall, thin man with close-cropped hair and a cleft chin, often dressing formally in button-up shirts and ties.

Coil's ambition and pride drive him to extreme lengths, using his power to torture people for information and stress relief in discarded timelines. He formed the Undersiders and employed various other villain groups to further his goals, ultimately orchestrating a plan to take over Brockton Bay by becoming the PRT Director. However, his deception was uncovered by Skitter, who confronted and killed him, putting an end to his schemes.]

[Battery, a member of the Brockton Bay Protectorate, gained her powers through a deal with Cauldron. Driven by guilt and a desire to prove herself, she goes above and beyond in her duties as a hero.

Battery wears a skintight white and dark grey costume with glowing cobalt blue circuit-like lines. She is described as being approximately 5'3" or 5'4" tall.

Her power allows her to charge up and release energy to boost her speed, strength, and electromagnetic abilities. While charged, she is nearly invincible and faster than her teammate and husband, Assault.

Battery's background includes being the daughter of a detective frustrated by the villain Madcap's escapes. After making a deal with Cauldron for powers, she captured Madcap on her eighth attempt, leading to his reformation as Assault. The two eventually married and transferred to Brockton Bay, where Battery briefly led the Wards before graduating to the Protectorate.

During the Slaughterhouse Nine's attack on Brockton Bay, Battery was poisoned by one of Bonesaw's spiders while tracking the villains. As she lay dying, she confessed her life and actions to her mentor, Legend, unaware of his own involvement with Cauldron.]

[The Cauldron Compound, a vast multifunctional complex spanning multiple dimensions, serves as the base of operations for the secretive organization known as Cauldron. Its spartan, white-tiled interior is eerily spotless and seemingly endless, with wings of the structure located on separate continents, connected only by the powers of the Doormaker.

The compound houses various facilities, including interview rooms for Cauldron customers, medical equipment for testing, and the personal offices of key members such as Doctor Mother and Number Man. The basement levels, not adhering to the white aesthetic, contain cells for Case 53s and other parahumans undergoing research.

Following the events of Gold Morning, the compound was briefly occupied by Teacher's group before being taken over by the Wardens. Despite the change in ownership, the Cauldron Compound remains a symbol of the organization's far-reaching influence and the morally ambiguous actions taken in the name of saving humanity.]

[Titans are parahumans who have undergone a broken second trigger, resulting in their shard taking full control over their body. These immensely powerful beings have access to the full capabilities of their shard, often surpassing the original host's abilities and exhibiting increased durability and reach. Titans vary greatly in appearance, with common elements including exaggerated hair, lack of facial features, and merged legs.

Psychologically, Titans are driven by their shard's alien goals, primarily focused on perpetuating the Entities' life-cycle by forming networks and accumulating energy to shatter their host planet across realities. The original human host's consciousness may persist within the Titan to varying degrees.

Titans emerged during the assault on the time bubbles, with Dauntless becoming the first known Titan. As reality began to unravel, more Titans formed, engaging in battles and forming networks as they sought to fulfill their shards' objectives. Despite the efforts of heroes and villains alike, the Titan threat persisted, with Titan Fortuna's network ultimately engaging in a confrontation with the Simurgh. The deployment of a parahuman plague created a stalemate, forcing the Titans to a standstill.]

["You were still a child, and you needed rules and a foundation to define yourself by, as any child does. Your chose your anchor, chose Scion, and you formed your view of capes as faerie to distance yourself from a world you barely felt in touch with. You built up your persona as Glaistig Uaine, a name others gave you. You craved structure."

Ciara, better known as Glaistig Uaine or the Faerie Queen, is a powerful parahuman with the ability to harvest and use the powers of deceased capes. Believed to have triggered at a young age and later experienced a second trigger event, Ciara's powers and isolation led her to develop a delusional worldview, seeing parahumans as "faerie" and Scion as a godlike figure.

With the appearance of a young girl in her early teens, Ciara speaks in an archaic manner, often with a chorus of broken voices. Her hair is blonde, and her eyes are green. In battle, she wears a cloak and robe that glitters green and black.

Feared by the cape community for her ability to permanently kill even the most powerful parahumans, Ciara was eventually imprisoned in the Birdcage, where she became a cell block leader. During Gold Morning, she played a crucial role in the fight against Scion, ultimately claiming Eidolon's power and becoming the most powerful parahuman in history. After the event, she began to re-examine her life with the help of therapy, presenting herself to the world as Valkyrie.]

[Cauldron's Vials, also known as formulas or samples, are the serums used by the secretive organization to grant powers to their clients and test subjects. These vials, about the size of a pen and contained in stainless steel canisters, hold a colored, metallic, semi-transparent liquid that, when consumed, causes intense pain followed by a trigger event.

The effects of the vials are influenced by the recipient's personality, mental state, and background. Cauldron carefully screens their clients to ensure the best possible outcomes. However, the vials can also cause physical and mental alterations, with more extreme cases resulting in monstrous deviations known as Case 53s.

Cauldron rates their vials using various qualities, most notably R (reliability), O (uniqueness), and P (PRT Classifications). Some notable vials include the Deus formula, which produced projection powers like those of Genesis and Siberian, and the Balance formula, which is mixed with most vials to reduce the risk of physical mutations.

The vials are produced from the broken-down body parts of the dead Entity, Eden. Many prominent parahumans, including members of Cauldron, the Triumvirate, and various heroes and villains, owe their powers to these formulas, making Cauldron's influence on the parahuman world far-reaching and profound.]

["I give people power, and I think there is a submissive kind of appeal to being a slave. To being numbed. Some fall for me like an alcoholic falls to drink. Love, after a fashion. In your case, that's almost a defense mechanism."

Benjamin Terrell, publicly known as Teacher, is a villainous mastermind and long-term planner who specializes in granting Thinker and Tinker powers to his thralls in exchange for their loyalty and subservience. A mundane-looking man with a red face, curly brown hair, and a beard, Teacher's appearance belies his cunning and manipulative nature.

Before his imprisonment in the Birdcage, Teacher organized high-profile assassinations, amassing a small army of empowered minions. His power allows him to grant a wide variety of abilities with a simple touch, with the recipient becoming susceptible to his influence. The strength of the granted power inversely correlates with the thrall's diminished faculties, creating a dynamic where the more information they possess, the less able they are to express it.

During Gold Morning, Teacher was released from the Birdcage and played a role in the fight against Scion, striking deals with Cauldron and temporarily controlling Dragon. Known for his supreme confidence and ability to set plans in motion that unfold years later, Teacher remains a formidable and enigmatic figure.]

[Broken triggers are a type of extremely violent trigger event first observed after Zion's death, in which shards appear to disobey their intended behavior, often leading to the deaths of their hosts and bystanders. Without the guidance of the entity's primary intelligence, individual shards can no longer coordinate with the greater network or alter their behaviors properly.

Broken triggers share some commonalities, such as disjointed trigger visions that may replay Zion's memories, and an almost shaker-like effect that allows the shard to jump from person to person, affecting multiple individuals. Those affected by broken triggers almost invariably die as a result of their powers or the trigger event itself, as the Manton Effect, which typically protects parahumans from their own powers, seems to be absent or greatly diminished.

The manifestation of broken triggers varies depending on the position within the 'area of effect,' with those farther from the center being less mobile. Powers generated by broken triggers often kill their hosts in gruesome ways, such as a fractal-like tree tearing away at the host's body or the host being buried by their own power. Broken triggers have become a common and devastating occurrence in the post-Gold Morning era.]

[Brockton Bay is a coastal city located in the northeastern United States. With a civilian population of around 350,000 prior to Leviathan's attack, Brockton Bay is situated north of Boston, bordered by the Atlantic Ocean to the east and mountains or hills to the west. The city's mild climate and unique geography make it an attractive location for parahumans, contributing to its high cape population.

Founded as a trading post and port during America's colonization, Brockton Bay's economy initially thrived on the shipping industry. However, as import/export businesses declined, the city faced a significant shift in its economic landscape. While the wealthy managed to adapt by investing in technology and banking, many former dock workers and laborers turned to illicit activities, leading to a boom in the local supervillain population during the late 1990s.

The city is home to various parahuman groups and organizations, including the Protectorate ENE, the Wards, New Wave, the Empire Eighty-Eight, the Azn Bad Boys, the Merchants, and the Undersiders. Throughout the story, Brockton Bay faces numerous challenges, including Bakuda's bombing campaign, Leviathan's devastating attack, and the Slaughterhouse Nine's recruitment drive.

Leviathan's assault on May 15, 2011, causes significant damage to the city, flooding downtown and southern areas and forming a sizable lake. The Endbringer attack also results in the loss of several prominent heroes, including members of New Wave. In the aftermath, the city becomes a target for the Slaughterhouse Nine and later suffers from Echidna's rampage.

Following the creation of a portal to Earth Gimel by Tattletale, Labyrinth, and Scrub, Brockton Bay gains newfound importance as an evacuation point during Scion's attack. The urban area on the Gimel side of the portal, known as New Brockton, becomes one of the origin settlements for The City.]

[I admit it, I admit I'm weaker, slower, my options are pretty limited in a fight. But I'm tenacious. I'm shameless, if I have to be, because I refuse to lose to you. And I find it pretty fucking poetic that I have the upper hand because of the very things that you capes look down on us for."

Emily Piggot, the former Director of the PRT ENE, is a stubborn and strong-willed woman with a deep distrust towards capes. As a PRT field agent, she survived the disastrous Nilbog mission, which left her with severe injuries and a jaded perspective on parahumans.

Piggot is described as an obese woman with steel-grey eyes and a bleached blonde bob-style haircut, usually seen wearing a navy blue jacket and skirt. Her injuries from the Nilbog mission left her dependent on hemodialysis and unable to exercise vigorously.

Despite her prejudices, Piggot remains committed to her duty of providing guidance and oversight to capes as the PRT Director. She is known for her no-nonsense attitude and unwavering resolve in the face of adversity. Piggot plays a crucial role in managing the Protectorate, Wards, and PRT agents in Brockton Bay, navigating the complex landscape of parahuman conflicts and politics.]

[While there are no direct speech quotes from James Tagg in Worm, his personality and actions speak volumes about his character.

James Tagg, a former soldier and PRT squad leader, was instated as the Director of PRT East-North-East following the death of Thomas Calvert. With a combative personality and a strong "us versus them" mentality, Tagg led the PRT on a warpath against the criminal element in Brockton Bay.

Tagg has black hair with heavily lined eyes and thick eyebrows, and his gruff voice reflects his history as a long-time smoker. He wears a matching wedding band with his wife, who shares his uncompromising views on criminals.

Known for his stubborn and unyielding nature, Tagg believes that eliminating criminals is a war and that the world is worse off with criminals winning. He is willing to go to great lengths to pressure villains, even threatening to subject Taylor's father to lengthy interrogations to gain leverage over her.

Tagg played a crucial role in the events following the Echidna incident, ordering Dragon and Defiant to confront Skitter at Arcadia and later attempting to kill her during an interrogation. His actions ultimately led to his death at the hands of Skitter's bugs, a testament to his unrelenting pursuit of what he believed to be justice.]

["The whole hero-villain thing isn't my area of expertise. I'm a psychologist, not a philosopher or a moralist. My focus is on the individual, not on the label. I want to know what drives you."

Dr. Jessica Yamada is a dedicated parahuman psychologist who worked for the Protectorate and other hero organizations. With eight years of training as a psychiatrist, she specializes in helping child parahumans navigate the complexities of their powers and the trauma they've experienced.

Known for her calm demeanor and ability to work with dangerous patients, Dr. Yamada is an expert in parahuman psychology, providing valuable insights into trigger events and the mental health of her clients. She disapproves of much of cape culture, particularly the use of codenames, believing that it dehumanizes her patients.

Dr. Yamada works with various clients, including the Brockton Bay Wards, Sveta, Victoria Dallon, and Weaver. She is not afraid to stand up to authority figures when necessary, prioritizing the well-being of her patients above all else.

As a consultant for the PRT, Dr. Yamada plays a crucial role in assessing and treating the psychological needs of parahumans. Her dedication, expertise, and compassionate approach make her an invaluable asset in the parahuman world.]

["Please. Do as Principal Howell is asking and form lines."

Adamant is a member of the New York Protectorate, serving under Legend before his transfer to Brockton Bay. As a ferrokinetic, Adamant is a heavy hitter capable of staying in the fight due to his Brute-like power application.

He wears a metallic costume featuring metal bands and panels loosely linked together by chains, fit over a black bodysuit. Adamant's power allows him to manipulate metal around himself with strong, crude movements for both offensive and defensive purposes. He can create large, rough weapons and form metal into crude armor to protect himself, although his metallokinesis focuses on strength rather than agility or accuracy.

Adamant participated in the fight against Leviathan in Brockton Bay and later returned to the city following the Echidna incident. He confronted Skitter and Hellhound during the incident at Arcadia High, going toe-to-toe with Hellhound's augmented dogs.
