As a natural trigger, Adamant remained with the Protectorate following the revelations about Cauldron. His role as a heavy-hitting Brute with the ability to manipulate metal makes him a valuable asset in combat situations, despite the limitations of his power's fine control and range.

["You're making me regret I didn't take that teaching job when I had the chance. I would've had to deal with a lot less of this."

Ethan, known publicly as Assault, is a member of the Brockton Bay Protectorate. Formerly a villain named Madcap, he operated as a jailbreak specialist before being caught by Battery and joining the heroes. As Assault, he wears red body armor with a visor covering the upper half of his face.

Assault is a kinetic energy manipulator, able to control the energies of movement, acceleration, and motion on himself and things he touches. This allows him to move at high speeds, deliver powerful kicks, and resist incoming attacks.

Smart, witty, and good with kids, Assault is a highly observant individual who continuously pestered Battery for a date before they eventually married. Despite his past as a villain, he has proven to be a valuable asset to the Protectorate.

Following the Slaughterhouse Nine's attack on Brockton Bay, which resulted in Battery's death, Assault blamed the Undersiders and pushed for a more aggressive approach against them. He continued to serve the Protectorate, participating in various battles and confrontations.]

[Challenger was a member of the Brockton Bay Protectorate, known for her reckless driving and intimidating appearance. She wore a red bodysuit with epaulettes and decorations, along with headgear featuring a diagonal blindfold covering one of her eyes, which she lost in an incident in a city other than Brockton Bay.

Although her powers are unknown, Challenger carried an axe and a rifle, both as tall as she was, and rode a motorcycle. She believed she was not good in front of cameras, likely due to her choice not to wear a mask in costume, instead taking more extreme measures to mask her identity as a civilian.

Challenger fought against Lung when he first arrived in Brockton Bay and was on the roster as of 2010 when Kid Win was a member of the Wards. However, she left the team before the events of Worm in April 2011, either transferring to a different city or passing away. Her tenure in the Brockton Bay Protectorate was marked by her fierce presence and unconventional approach to heroism.]

["You're right. I was, am, angry. At the pointlessness of what happened, what's still happening out there. I get frustrated and angry when I'm here, because I feel like I should be out on the streets. I get pissed off when I'm out on patrol because I feel like I should be with my family… but when I'm with my family, I feel frustrated and helpless because I can't do anything there…"

Dennis, widely known as the young hero Clockblocker, is a member of the Brockton Bay Wards. He triggered at age 15 while donating bone marrow to his father, who was dying of cancer. Clockblocker's power allows him to "tag" nearly anything, freezing it in time for a period between 30 seconds and 10 minutes.

Clockblocker wears a skintight white costume with panels of glossy white armoring and grey clocks inscribed on it. His helmet is a faceless, smooth expanse of white. He is Caucasian with red hair, blue eyes, and about average height.

Known for his humor and tendency to joke about everything, Clockblocker deliberately chose an offensive cape name because he found it funny. Despite his lighthearted demeanor, he is deeply affected by his father's illness and the stress of being a hero.

Clockblocker plays a crucial role in various battles, including the fight against Leviathan, the Slaughterhouse Nine, and Echidna. His power proves invaluable in turning the tide of these conflicts, and he develops a unique dynamic with the villain Skitter.]

[All-or-Nothing is a threat-assessment term used by the PRT to refer to capes with highly potent powers that break the rules other parahumans follow. These powers are often absolute in nature, violating physics and surpassing the consequences faced by other capes.

Examples of All-or-Nothing capes include Clockblocker, who can freeze anything in time; the Siberian, an invulnerable projection; and Flechette, who can imbue objects with the ability to pierce anything. When two All-or-Nothing effects come into contact, they mutually nullify each other.

All-or-Nothing powers are crucial in fighting Endbringers and other seemingly invincible threats. However, they are not always linked to a cape's overall threat level, as some All-or-Nothing capes have limitations that hinder their effectiveness.

On Earth Bet, All-or-Nothing powers play a significant role in various battles, including the fights against Leviathan, the Slaughterhouse Nine, Echidna, and Behemoth. Their unique properties make them both invaluable assets and formidable challenges.]

["I could skip that one for the fight that comes after. And the one that comes after that. We don't know if my power has a limit, but it's possible it does, and the time I supposedly buy ends up being for nothing. This is my city, Addison. A city with you in it. With Jennifer. With your friends, your teachers the places you love. There's never going to be a place that I'll step up to defend faster or with more conviction than our city."

Shawn, publicly known as Dauntless, was a member of the Brockton Bay Protectorate with the ability to slowly grant powers to items in his possession. He wears gold and white armor with a Greek-style helmet, wielding an empowered spear, shield, and boots.

Dauntless triggered after performing a C-section on his girlfriend, Kelly, during a mudslide to save their son, Addison. His meteoric rise in the Protectorate led to resentment from Armsmaster, as it was widely believed that Dauntless might eventually replace him as leader.

During the Battle at the Gallery, Dauntless confronted the Undersiders, demonstrating the capabilities of his empowered items. However, he was later frozen in time by Leviathan during the Endbringer's attack on Brockton Bay.

Known for his strong sense of duty and commitment to protecting his city, Dauntless was a popular hometown hero in Brockton Bay, with many speculating that his powers could eventually rival those of the Triumvirate.]

[Dovetail is an itinerant member of the Protectorate, known for her ability to fly, carry people, and leave trails of luminous slivers of light that fall to the ground in her wake. These slivers balloon out to create soft forcefields that encase those they come into contact with, impeding movement.

Wearing a costume with a high collar and a built-in containment foam sprayer, Dovetail traditionally uses her power to hover over a target, reinforcing her forcefields until the PRT arrives to subdue them.

During the Boston Games, Dovetail was dispatched to reinforce the local heroes and sent after the Woad Giant. Following the Battle against Echidna, she was sent to join the Brockton Bay Protectorate as they needed reinforcements.

In a confrontation with Skitter, Dovetail demonstrated her skill in maneuvering to prevent her slivers of light from harming those below. Despite her best efforts, Skitter managed to outmaneuver her using her swarm and silk.]

[Sere is an itinerant member of the Protectorate with the ability to violently draw in moisture from his environment, allowing him to stun or kill targets while ignoring forcefields and armor. His power manifests as a pale nimbus of mist surrounding him, which he can use in a long, tight cone-shaped "blast" or a tight field around him.

Wearing white desert-tribal style robes with fine patterning and a featureless mask with light blue lenses, Sere was sent to join the Brockton Bay Protectorate after the Battle against Echidna to serve as a counter to Skitter's abilities.

In a confrontation at Arcadia High, Sere initially had success against Skitter but was quickly adapted to and incapacitated by the teenage villain. He was caught again during Skitter's retaliatory strike on the PRT before he could engage her personally.

Despite his brutal effectiveness, Sere benefited from the Protectorate's PR to avoid being labeled a villain. He assisted Kid Win in creating drones adapted to use his abilities and patrolled with Dovetail following Skitter's surrender.]

["He was no longer that selfish teenager who'd received superpowers from his father like his peers got cars on their sixteenth birthday. He'd hoped for an undetectable, undeniable advantage over his peers and been enraged when it had been denied him. He'd changed, forced himself to change; he would be a good student, he'd help his fellow citizens, do the right thing."

Rory Christner, also known as Triumph, is a member of the Brockton Bay Protectorate. His father gave him a vial that enhanced his strength, speed, and capabilities, but it also ruined his dreams of playing Major League baseball. Disappointed, Rory joined the Brockton Bay Wards in 2008, serving as captain for a few years before graduating to the Protectorate.

Triumph's costume has a gladiator/lion theme, with a gold lion helm, shoulder pads, belt, and a skintight suit. His main power is sound manipulation, allowing him to control its force and area of effect. He also has a mild healing factor and some level of super-strength.

Throughout the story, Triumph faces off against various threats, including the Undersiders, the Slaughterhouse Nine, and Noelle. Despite his initial selfishness, he strives to be a good hero and protect his city.]

["Velocity's name filled in the blank beside an event at a conference with Maine state law enforcement. No reason given for that. A long way to travel, maybe."

Robin Swoyer, known publicly as Velocity, is a member of the Brockton Bay Protectorate. He enlisted in the military hoping to learn languages and travel, but found himself stuck in the rank and file. After triggering in a bad situation, he joined the Protectorate, happy to have an 'out' from military service.

As Velocity, Robin wears a red costume with racing stripes down either side and two stripes meeting in a 'v' on his chest. His power allows him to change 'states' by altering the way time or physics work in relation to himself, speeding up at the cost of reduced ability to affect the world.

During the Battle at the Gallery, Velocity engaged Bitch and her dogs before being taken down by Skitter's pepper spray and a baton between the legs. He worked with Trickster to rescue people during Leviathan's attack but tragically lost his life when the Crater Lake was created.]

["Be quiet, Aegis. Your trying to speak with a punctured lung physically pains me, and as much as I admire standing up for your team, your one lungful of breath is wasted here."

Carlos, known publicly as Aegis, is a parahuman and a member of the Brockton Bay Wards. Of Puerto Rican descent, he wears a rust-red costume with silver-white trim and a shield emblem. His power grants him flight and an augmented physiology that operates at peak capacity as long as he is alive, making him extremely difficult to put down.

As the leader of the Brockton Bay Wards, Aegis is recognized as capable and intelligent by both his teammates and the criminal elements in the city. During the battle at the Bank, he switched costumes with Clockblocker in an attempt to fool the Undersiders, but was severely injured by Hellhound's dogs.

Aegis fought against the Empire Eighty-Eight and participated in the battle against Leviathan. Tragically, he was killed by the Endbringer when it escaped containment, his body smashed beyond the point of recovery.]

["Weld's a boy scout, Sveta. He's probably in my bottom ten people to go to if I want deception and acting ability."

Weld is a Case 53 and member of the Boston Wards who was brought in to lead the Brockton Bay Wards after Leviathan's attack. His body is entirely composed of various metals, granting him enhanced strength, durability, and the ability to alter his shape and composition.

Despite his imposing appearance, Weld is an accepting and trusting individual, known for his respectful, honest, and kind demeanor. He struggles with the changes his body has undergone, relying on music as a coping mechanism.

As a leader, Weld proved to be competent and analytical, successfully guiding the Brockton Bay Wards through perilous situations. He formed a close relationship with Director Armstrong, who became a father figure to him.

During the fight against Leviathan and the subsequent confrontations with the Slaughterhouse Nine and Echidna, Weld demonstrated his leadership skills and unwavering determination to protect his fellow heroes and the city.]

[Crucible is the post-timeskip team leader of the Brockton Bay Wards. As a relatively inexperienced leader, he often defers to authority figures like Chevalier and struggles with not knowing the details of classified events. Despite this, he demonstrates endurance and selflessness in his role as a hero.

Crucible's costume leaves his jaw exposed, and his power allows him to create pale blue forcefield bubbles that can flare with intense heat, incinerating everything inside. He hides the lethal aspect of his power to maintain his heroic reputation.

Recruited to the Brockton Bay Protectorate after the battle against Echidna, Crucible was present during key events such as Skitter's surrender and her decision to join the heroes as Weaver. He later led the Wards during the fight against the Slaughterhouse 9000, facing numerous cloned villains and sustaining injuries in the process. It was during this battle that he first used his power to kill, burning several murderous clones to death.]

["What the fuck is he doing here? We crossed paths with him once, Regent and Bitch beat him. Either he's here for revenge or he's joined the Wards very, very recently. My power's suggesting it's the latter."

Browbeat, a member of the Brockton Bay Wards, possesses two mutually reinforcing powers: short-range telekinesis and biokinesis. His telekinesis acts as a personal force field, enhancing his strength and durability, while his biokinesis allows him to shape his body into a muscular physique and heal his wounds.

In his cape identity, Browbeat wears a dark blue spandex costume with a diamond print and a full-face mask. As a civilian, he is described as moderately handsome.

Browbeat's early solo hero career involved testing his abilities against various villains, including the Undersiders, before joining the Wards for training and support. Despite his powers, he tends to avoid conflict, a trait shared with his parents.

Browbeat participates in the fight against the Undersiders at the bank and later battles Leviathan when the Endbringer attacks Brockton Bay, tragically losing his life in the process.]

["Let's put vendettas aside. We have bigger fish to fry. But it's not my place to talk tactics. I'm just the rookie. The messenger."

Trevor Medina, known as Chariot, is a teenage Tinker who specializes in mobility, movement, and transportation. Lanky with big ears, close-shorn hair, and a narrow, triangular face, Trevor is a black youth with the beginnings of a teenage beard.

As Chariot, he wears an ever-evolving suit of power armor equipped with roller skates, a jetpack, and various other mobility-enhancing devices. Initially struggling with a lack of resources, Trevor was recruited by Coil over a year before the story's events.

Posing as a new member of the Brockton Bay Wards, Chariot acted as a mole for Coil, feeding information to the villain while maintaining his cover. During the fight against the Slaughterhouse Nine, he delivered a message from the PRT Director to Tattletale, showcasing his role as a double agent.

Chariot's betrayal was revealed when he detonated his flight pack during Coil's attack on a town hall meeting, wounding many heroes in the process. Despite his technical skills, Trevor's loyalty ultimately lay with Coil, making him a dangerous and unpredictable adversary.]

["I'm not good at being alone. I found that out a while ago, and what's happened these past few weeks, they only made it clearer. I need company, and your company is what I want the most. I can't say it'll be forever, but for now…"

Lily, also known as Flechette and later Foil, is a Japanese-American girl with the ability to imbue nonliving material with the power to ignore select laws of physics, allowing it to punch through virtually anything. Originally a member of the New York Wards, she was transferred to Brockton Bay following Leviathan's attack.

As Flechette, she wore a deep purple costume with white armor panels and carried a Tinker-made arbalest that launched empowered needles. Her secondary power grants her an intuitive understanding of angles and timing, enhancing her accuracy.

Lily triggered as part of a group trigger involving her estranged sister and March, who would become her nemesis. Despite her hopes of befriending Shadow Stalker, Lily was shocked by the other Ward's comfort with violence. She eventually left the Wards and joined the Undersiders, starting a relationship with Parian.

During the fight against Scion, Foil's power proved crucial, as her charged attacks could bypass his defenses and open a hole to his true body, leading to his defeat.]

["When it came to his teammates and the PRT staff, he could read their emotions and he could sense the degree to which they cared and didn't care. Through some combination of that and his unwillingness to show weakness that might see him getting less shifts, responsibilities and power, he didn't tell them when he was hurt, hurting, or scared."

Dean Stansfield, known publicly as Gallant, was a member of the Brockton Bay Wards and the on-again, off-again boyfriend of Victoria Dallon. As Gallant, he wore a futuristic set of silver and gunmetal colored power armor, pretending to be a Tinker in public.

Dean was an empath capable of sensing emotions and generating concussive blasts of energy that could alter emotions in addition to packing a punch. He was the heir of his wealthy parents' company and moved in the same circles as the Anders family.

Despite his gentlemanly demeanor, Dean struggled with the emotional weight of his powers and his unwillingness to show weakness. He had a good relationship with Victoria and hoped to help Amy with her emotional state, but never got the chance.

Tragically, Dean was killed during Leviathan's attack on Brockton Bay, his final thoughts being of Victoria and his foreboding realization that he had not told anyone how close Amy was to a mental breakdown.]

["Follow the law. When the law isn't available, do what's right. When what's right isn't clear, ask for help."

Victoria Dallon, known publicly as Glory Girl, is a prominent hero and a member of New Wave. As the daughter of Carol and Mark Dallon and the adoptive sister of Amy Dallon, Victoria is a hot-tempered and prideful cape who genuinely believes in helping others.

With platinum blonde hair and a white costume featuring a skirt, shorts, cape, boots, and a golden tiara, Victoria cuts an impressive figure. Her powers include flight, invincibility through a forcefield, superhuman strength, and an aura that inspires awe in allies and intimidation in enemies.

Victoria is protective of her family and enjoys fighting, sometimes using excessive force. She dated Dean Stansfield (Gallant) and hoped to marry him someday. After his death during Leviathan's attack, Victoria was left adrift.

Following the Slaughterhouse Nine's assault on Brockton Bay, Victoria was mutilated by Crawler's venom. In a desperate attempt to help, Panacea transformed her into a monstrous conglomeration of body parts. Traumatized by this violation and confined to the Parahuman Asylum, Victoria struggled to cope with her new reality.

Despite her challenges, Victoria fought in the final battle against Scion, playing a crucial role. Though Amy restored her body, Victoria was left to grapple with the emotional fallout of her experiences.]

["His disability or disabilities put him a step behind the rest. His daydreaming was worse, because his thoughts were so damn interesting, now. Couldn't finish half his projects without feeling compelled to move on to something else."

Chris, known as Kid Win, is a teenage member of the Brockton Bay Wards. Diagnosed with ADD and dyscalculia before gaining his powers, Chris struggles to focus on his Tinker projects, often leaving them unfinished. With brown hair and a pale complexion, he wears red and gold body armor with a red visor as his costume.

As a Tinker, Chris specializes in modular devices, initially believing his specialty was advanced guns. He greatly respects Hero and models himself after the legendary Tinker. Despite his challenges, Chris manages to create impressive devices, such as a hoverboard and the powerful Alternator Cannon.

Kid Win participates in various battles and events, including the fight against Leviathan, the confrontation with the Travelers, and the action to stop Coil's strike on the debate. Post-timeskip, he focuses on expanding his specialty.

During Gold Morning, Kid Win fights alongside other heroes but tragically loses his life when he is struck by a laser and something inside his suit detonates.]

["Something you should know about me. The reason I'm such a good runner? It's not that I'm driven to win. It's that I really, really hate losing. And I hate losing the most when it's to a depressing queef like you."

Sophia Hess, known as the vigilante Shadow Stalker, is a mean-spirited and violent member of the Brockton Bay Wards. With dark skin, long hair, and a slender, athletic build, Sophia is a track and field star who triggered at age 12. Her power allows her to shift into a "shadow state," passing through walls and making her lightweight.

As Shadow Stalker, Sophia wears a black cloak and bodysuit with a metal mask resembling a stern woman's face. She carries two crossbows with lethal and nonlethal bolts. Sophia's aggressive personality is influenced by her shard, leading her to despise weakness and enjoy violence.

In her civilian life, Sophia is Emma Barnes' best friend and one of Taylor Hebert's main bullies. After being caught by the Wards, Sophia is given probationary status but continues to use lethal bolts and bully others. Her secret identity is eventually revealed, leading to her being sent to juvenile detention.]

[Emma Barnes, once the best friend of Taylor Hebert, became one of her most vicious bullies after a traumatic assault by ABB members. Determined to purge all weakness from her life, Emma turned on Taylor, using her intimate knowledge of Taylor's insecurities to psychologically torture her former friend.

A tall, curvy redhead with a talent for modeling, Emma relished the attention and popularity her looks and charisma brought her. She formed a close friendship with Sophia Hess and, along with Madison Clements, subjected Taylor to a brutal bullying campaign that eventually led to Taylor's trigger event.

Emma's worldview was shattered when Taylor was revealed to be the powerful supervillain Skitter. Forced to confront the consequences of her actions, Emma tried to slander Taylor to investigators but found herself increasingly isolated and stressed.

During Gold Morning, Emma refused to leave her room to evacuate and died when Scion destroyed her family's home. Taylor, upon learning of Emma's death, felt little emotion and rejected the Barnes family's attempts to blame her for their daughter's fate.]

[Toggle is a young female member of the post-timeskip Brockton Bay Wards. As the youngest on her team, she is somewhat naive and likes to make jokes, once wondering if there is porn of Case 53s.

Toggle wears layered body armor featuring circles of light that shine in changing colors. She carries a mace or baton that glows with the same pattern as her armor.

Her power involves creating "five shadowy silhouettes" of herself that sit around her. When striking an enemy, lights flare from her silhouettes. Although not particularly effective against certain threats like Breed or Murder Rat, her teammate Crucible suggests she would be more useful in other situations.

During the fight against the Slaughterhouse 9000, Toggle worked alongside Weaver, the Undersiders, and her fellow Wards and Protectorate members. She sustained a shoulder wound during the battle. Toggle also participated in the fight against clones of Skinslip, Hatchet Face, Miasma, and Murder Rat at Redfield.

As Gold Morning began, Toggle watched the destruction of Great Britain on the screens of the Dragonfly alongside her teammates and the Undersiders.]

["We all have baggage. We could all die at any time, that's life as a cape. Put those things together and if we wait to get over our baggage we're liable to end up dead before we get anywhere."

Missy Biron, known as Vista, is a strong-willed and confident member of the Brockton Bay Wards. Despite being the youngest on the team, Vista's power and experience make her a formidable hero. Her ability to distort space allows her to stretch, compress, or bend non-living material, with her power growing stronger the longer she stays in an area.

Vista wears a costume with a skirt featuring wavy white and forest green lines, body armor panels, and a green visor. She has wavy dark-blonde hair that she straightens when in costume. Vista triggered due to her parents' divorce and hostile relationship, leading her to find solace in her identity as a Ward.

Vista faces numerous challenges, including the deaths of her teammates and the Slaughterhouse Nine. She forms strong bonds with her fellow Wards, particularly Gallant and Weld, and even develops a friendship with the villain Bitch. Despite her age, Vista's determination and skill make her a respected and feared hero in Brockton Bay.]

["We have no secrets. That's the whole fucking point of our team. Heroes with no secret identities, no secrets, full disclosure, total accountability."

New Wave, originally known as the Brockton Bay Brigade, is a family-based hero team operating in Brockton Bay. The group consists of the Pelham and Dallon families, each with their own unique powers. New Wave is known for its commitment to public accountability, with all members openly revealing their identities and eschewing masks.

The team was founded by siblings Lady Photon, Brandish, and Lightstar, along with their partners. After unmasking and rebranding as New Wave, they gained national attention but suffered a devastating blow when Fleur was assassinated. This tragedy led to Lightstar's departure and stalled the team's growth.

New Wave faces numerous challenges, including the Endbringer attack that claims the lives of Manpower and Shielder. The incarceration of Panacea and Glory Girl following the Slaughterhouse Nine's assault further fractures the team. Despite these setbacks, the remaining members continue to fight for justice in Brockton Bay, embodying their ideals of transparency and accountability.]

[Sarah Pelham, known as Lady Photon or Photon Mom, is the leader of New Wave, a family-based hero team in Brockton Bay. With the ability to fly, create energy blasts, and generate forcefields, Sarah is a formidable hero. She wears a white bodysuit featuring a starburst emblem that changes color from indigo to purple.

Described as an attractive woman with blonde hair and a heart-shaped face, Sarah is a dedicated parent and cape. She dislikes the nickname "Photon Mom" given to her by the media. Sarah triggered alongside her sister, Brandish, when they were kidnapped as children.

Sarah faces numerous challenges, including the deaths of her husband, Manpower, and son, Shielder, during the battle against Leviathan. Despite these losses, she continues to lead New Wave and fight for justice in Brockton Bay. During Gold Morning, Sarah was part of Khepri's swarm and tragically killed by Scion before Khepri could react.]
entries.comment: Lady Photon, Photon Mom, Sarah Pelham

entries.content:
["So many long hours spent around sick people, and I got numb to it, I stopped caring. Do you know how many hours I've spent awake at night, wishing my powers would just go away, or that some circumstance would come up where I'd make some excusable mistake where they would eventually forgive me, but where I couldn't visit the hospitals anymore?"

Amy Dallon, also known as Panacea, is a powerful biokinetic and member of New Wave. With the ability to heal and modify biology with a touch, Amy is considered one of the greatest healers in the world. She has frizzy brown hair, freckles, and a mousy appearance, wearing a white robe with a red cross when operating as Panacea.

Despite her incredible powers, Amy is deeply unhappy and struggles with immense guilt and loneliness. Her adoptive mother, Carol, is cold towards her, while her adoptive father, Mark, suffers from depression. Amy harbors a secret love for her sister, Victoria, which leads to disastrous consequences when she breaks her own rules and alters Victoria's mind.

Following her breakdown and the revelation of her secrets, Amy voluntarily goes to the Birdcage, where she meets her biological father, Marquis. During Gold Morning, she is released and plays a crucial role in the fight against Scion by modifying Taylor into Khepri.]

[Mark Dallon, known as Flashbang, is the husband of Carol Dallon, father of Victoria Dallon, and adoptive father of Amy Dallon. As a member of New Wave, he wears a white costume with padding, a helmet, and a green-yellow grenade icon. His power allows him to create orbs of light that detonate either concussively or explosively.

Mark suffers from clinical depression, which often leaves him feeling incompetent and out of his depth. Despite his efforts to be a good father, his condition hinders his ability to connect with his family, particularly his adoptive daughter, Amy.

Flashbang participates in various conflicts alongside New Wave, including the battles against the ABB, Empire Eighty-Eight, and Leviathan. However, he sustains a severe head injury during the Leviathan fight, leaving him bedridden. When Bonesaw attacks the Dallon household to recruit Panacea, Mark fights back and ultimately mercy kills a mutated Mouse Protector.

During Gold Morning, Flashbang appears visibly grim when Marquis is released from the Birdcage but does not participate in the fighting against Scion alongside the other members of New Wave.]

["It felt weird to tell my fourteen year old daughter to break a man's arm, once upon a time. We adapt."

Carol Dallon, known as Brandish, is the wife of Mark Dallon, mother of Victoria Dallon, and adoptive mother of Amy Dallon. As a member of New Wave, she wears a white costume with orange trim and a crossed-blade symbol. Her power allows her to create weapons and shields out of hard light and condense herself into an invincible, untouchable ball of light.

Carol is a skilled lawyer but struggles with severe trust issues stemming from her trigger event, where she was kidnapped and nearly executed. She is constantly wary of her adoptive daughter, Amy, and favors her biological daughter, Victoria.

Brandish participates in various battles alongside New Wave, including fights against the E88, Leviathan, and the Slaughterhouse Nine. Following the deaths of several New Wave members and her husband's head injury, Carol considers disbanding the team.

After discovering that Amy had used her powers to mutilate Victoria, Carol loses both of her daughters—Amy to the Birdcage and Victoria to the Parahuman Asylum. During Gold Morning, she briefly reunites with them before the final battle against Scion begins.]

[One of the bigger collections of racists above the bible belt. Quite possibly the biggest congregation of racist supervillains. The day Empire Eighty-Eight had gotten its name hadn't been a good day for our city."

The Empire Eighty-Eight, or E88, is a powerful gang of white supremacists based in Brockton Bay. Led by the ruthless Kaiser, the group is known for its hatred and violence towards non-whites. The E88 has a hierarchical structure, with various lieutenants serving beneath Kaiser, and it maintains connections to other racist organizations across North America.

The E88 clashes with rival gangs and the authorities. After Lung's capture, they attempt to expand their territory, only to face setbacks when Coil leaks the civilian identities of their capes to the public. The battle against Leviathan proves to be a turning point, as Kaiser is killed and the group splinters into two factions: Fenrir's Chosen and The Pure.

With roughly twenty capes in its roster, the E88 is a formidable force. Notable members include the former leader Allfather, the powerful Purity, the deadly Hookwolf, and the young but dangerous Rune. Despite its strength, the E88 ultimately crumbles under the weight of internal strife and external pressure.]

[The Azn Bad Boys (ABB) is a notorious gang based in the Docks area of Brockton Bay, known for its red and green colors. Led by the powerful parahuman Lung, the ABB forcefully recruits young Asians in the city, regardless of their specific ethnicity. The gang engages in various criminal activities, including theft, protection rackets, and human trafficking.

Despite having fewer capes than their rivals, the Empire Eighty-Eight, the ABB is considered equally dangerous due to the abilities of Lung and his lieutenant, Oni Lee. The gang's power dynamic shifts when Lung is briefly incarcerated, allowing the ruthless Tinker Bakuda to take control. Under her leadership, the ABB's tactics become even more brutal, involving forced recruitment, implanted bombs, and a campaign of terror against the city.

Ultimately, the ABB's actions prompt the city's other villain groups to form a temporary alliance, leading to the arrest of Lung and Bakuda and the gang's dissolution. The ABB serves as a significant antagonist, showcasing the destructive potential of unchecked parahuman influence in the criminal underworld.]

["I dislike the idea of being a follower, little Skitter. I maintain a territory, always. I bring my enemies low, and I am feared and respected, always. I enjoy the things I enjoy, drinking, food, fucking women. Never being fully out of control. You understand?"

Lung, born Kenta, is a notorious villain and the former leader of the Azn Bad Boys (ABB) in Brockton Bay. A tall, muscular half-Chinese, half-Japanese man with an ornate dragon mask and extensive tattoos, Lung has the ability to gradually transform into a dragon-like creature, becoming stronger, tougher, and gaining pyrokinesis the longer he fights.

Driven by a desire for power and control, Lung is a proud and brutal leader, commanding fear and respect through his strength and reputation. Despite his ruthless nature, he follows a code of conduct and believes in the power of fear to maintain his position.

Lung clashes with various heroes and villains, most notably Skitter, who becomes his nemesis. He is eventually defeated and sent to the Birdcage, where he becomes a key player in the prison's power dynamics. During Gold Morning, Lung is released to fight against Scion, showcasing his immense power as he goes toe-to-toe with the entity.]

[Oni Lee, one of Lung's lieutenants in the Azn Bad Boys (ABB), is a mysterious and feared villain known for his distinctive demon mask and sociopathic tendencies. His power allows him to teleport, leaving behind short-lived duplicates of himself that turn to ash, granting him a form of pseudo-immortality in combat.

Dressed in a black bodysuit with a belt and bandoleer of knives and grenades, Oni Lee's crimson mask with leering, fanged grin strikes terror into his enemies. His exact appearance beneath the mask remains unknown.

Oni Lee serves as a loyal enforcer for Lung, participating in various conflicts against the Undersiders and other rival gangs. He plays a crucial role in helping Lung escape from PRT custody during Bakuda's bombing spree.

Following Leviathan's attack on Brockton Bay, Oni Lee is found by the Slaughterhouse Nine. Bonesaw ultimately transforms him into a monstrous amalgamation with Hatchet Face, dubbed "Hack Job," trapping Oni Lee's consciousness within a body he cannot control. This tragic fate highlights the brutal and unforgiving nature of the Earth Bet, as even the most fearsome villains can fall victim to the machinations of others.]

["Even a small victory on our end is going to get a big reaction from her. Ego-wise, she's got a glass jaw. Hard to say if a win for us would mean she goes manic and blows everything up, or if she'd just crumple, but I guarantee she wouldn't handle it well."

Bakuda, a half-Asian, half-Caucasian tinker and member of the Azn Bad Boys (ABB), specializes in creating bombs with a wide variety of effects. Arrogant and theatrical, she wears a metal gas mask with opaque goggles and a braided cord of black, yellow, and green wires over her shoulders.

Bakuda triggered after a blow to her ego, possibly related to her academic struggles at Cornell University. She joined the ABB after being recruited by Lung, becoming one of his lieutenants and later taking over leadership during his imprisonment.

Bakuda clashes with the Undersiders and other heroes, using her implanted cranial bombs to control her underlings and unleashing a devastating bombing campaign on Brockton Bay. Her actions ultimately lead to her capture and imprisonment in the Birdcage, where she is eventually killed by Lung for her failure and disrespect.

As a tinker, Bakuda's ability to create powerful and versatile explosives, including a city-destroying EMP bomb, makes her a formidable villain. However, her arrogance and lack of common sense prove to be her undoing, highlighting the dangerous and unpredictable nature of tinkers.]

[Palanquin, initially known as Faultline's Crew, is a group of supervillains-for-hire led by the enigmatic Faultline. The team consists of several Case 53s, including Gregor the Snail, Newter, and Shamrock, as well as the powerful Shaker Labyrinth and the pyrokinetic Spitfire. The group's primary goal is to uncover the origins of the Case 53s while taking on mercenary work, with a strict code of never fighting without pay and avoiding murder.

Palanquin is involved in various conflicts and alliances, participating in the battle against the ABB, clashing with the Merchants, and assisting in the fight against Echidna. The team's reputation for professionalism and effectiveness is well-established, with a track record surpassing that of the Undersiders.

Palanquin's search for answers leads them to confront Cauldron, the shadowy organization responsible for the creation of the Case 53s. Despite the dangers they face, including an attack by the powerful Contessa, the group remains committed to their cause and their mercenary work, proving to be a formidable presence.

[The Archer's Bridge Merchants, commonly known as the Merchants, are a small-time supervillain gang in Brockton Bay, focused primarily on drug dealing and petty crime. Led by the villainous Skidmark, the gang initially had no real aspirations beyond getting rich through their illicit activities, using their powers only to make their work less risky.

The Merchants' roster includes Skidmark, who can create force fields that push objects in a single direction; Squealer, a vehicle tinker; Mush, a changer who can gather debris to form a giant body; and Trainwreck, a Case-53 tinker who creates steam-powered suits.

Following the chaos caused by Leviathan's attack on Brockton Bay and the collapse of the city's other major gangs, the Merchants seize the opportunity to expand their territory and influence. They begin holding dangerous gladiatorial matches to trigger and recruit new parahumans, including Scrub and Whirlygig.

Despite their sudden growth, the Merchants are ultimately wiped out by the Slaughterhouse Nine during one of their rallies, with most of their members killed in the attack. The gang's brief rise and fall showcase the brutal and opportunistic nature of the criminal underworld.]

[The Undersiders are a group of teenage supervillains operating in Brockton Bay, brought together by the mysterious Coil. Initially focused on robbery and escape, the team's dynamic shifts with the addition of Skitter, who pushes them towards more aggressive tactics. The group's members include:
- Grue, the original leader with the power to generate sensory-depriving darkness
- Tattletale, the cunning thinker who can extrapolate information and guide the team
- Bitch, who can empower dogs into monstrous sizes
- Regent, able to interfere with others' nervous systems
- Skitter, who can control arthropods within a wide radius
- Imp, Grue's sister, who can make people forget her existence
The Undersiders face numerous challenges, including conflicts with rival gangs, the Endbringer Leviathan, and the Slaughterhouse Nine. They eventually betray and kill their employer, Coil, taking over his criminal empire and becoming the dominant power in Brockton Bay's underworld.

The team's goals evolve, with members like Skitter joining the heroes and the group working to maintain peace in the city. The Undersiders' journey showcases the complexities of the hero-villain dynamic and the bonds formed between unlikely allies in the face of adversity.]

["That's the thing. What I'm thinking is… maybe when her power gave her the ability to understand dogs, it overwrote something else? Fucked up her ability to deal with people?"

Rachel Lindt, known as Bitch to her allies and Hellhound to her enemies, is a member of the Undersiders with the power to enhance dogs to monstrous sizes. Abandoned by her mother and failed by the foster system, Rachel triggered at a young age, forever altering her ability to understand and communicate with humans.

With a squarish, blunt-featured face, thick eyebrows, and auburn hair, Rachel is muscular and inclined to fitness. She wears heavy jackets with fur collars and dollar store dog masks, later donning a mask resembling one of her enhanced dogs, Brutus.

Struggling with social interaction and empathy, Rachel approaches many relationships as a dominance struggle. Fiercely loyal to her dogs and those she trusts, she has a skewed perception of family dynamics and often resorts to violence when threatened.

Rachel plays a crucial role in the Undersiders' battles, including the fights against Leviathan and the Slaughterhouse Nine. Despite her rough exterior, she forms close bonds with her teammates, particularly Taylor, and works to create a better life for herself and her ever-growing pack of dogs.]

["That's the way it always goes. I get close to people, and I don't want to lose that, so I go too far, and I push them away."

Brian Laborn, known as Grue, is a member of the Undersiders with the power to generate sensory-depriving darkness. Triggered by his desire to protect his sister from his mother's abusive boyfriend, Brian became a small-time villain before joining the Undersiders.

Tall, muscular, and handsome, Brian is an African-American teenager with cornrows. As Grue, he wears motorcycle leathers and a skull-faced helmet that allows his darkness to flow out for dramatic effect.

Brian is cautious, professional, and values his independence. He appreciates practicality and tries to keep his emotions in check. Despite his villainous status, he cares deeply for his teammates and sister, often shouldering burdens to protect them.

Throughout the story, Grue serves as the Undersiders' leader, guiding them through conflicts with rival gangs and the authorities. His darkness proves invaluable in battles against the likes of Lung, Leviathan, and the Slaughterhouse Nine. Brian's relationship with Taylor is a focal point, evolving from a sibling-like bond to a romantic connection.

After undergoing a second trigger event, Grue's powers expand to include a Trump ability, allowing him to copy the powers of others within his darkness. He continues to play a crucial role in the Undersiders' growth and their eventual control over Brockton Bay's criminal underworld.]

["Sucks to fade into the background, let me tell you. Not even talking about my power. It really… sucks. And I think, you know, I'm not very good at taking care of people. You lot excepted, almost all of those people who mattered are gone, one way or another."

Aisha Laborn, known as Imp, is the younger sister of Brian Laborn and a member of the Undersiders. Triggered by an encounter with armed men while out with her father, Aisha gained the power to become unnoticeable, causing others to forget her presence.

A beautiful African-American teenager with high cheekbones, a long neck, and a purple streak in her hair, Aisha dresses in a "trashy" yet vibrant style. As Imp, she wears a pale grey demon mask with slanted black lenses and a black scarf.

Insolent, rebellious, and immature, Aisha shares a similar personality to Regent. She dislikes authority figures but is fiercely protective of those she cares about. Her power both fits and clashes with her personality, as she resents being ignored but finds solace in the ability to escape difficult situations.

Imp proves to be a valuable asset to the Undersiders, using her power to gather information and assist in various missions. Despite her rough exterior, she deeply cares for her brother and teammates, particularly Regent, and works to protect their legacy in the face of adversity.]

["I don't- I didn't want this. I knew I'd be forced to fight, but I thought it would be a situation like this, not a- not me being the aggressor."

Sabah, known as Parian, is a Middle-Eastern immigrant and rogue cape operating in Brockton Bay. Triggered by the stress of an unwanted admirer and her father's death, Parian gained the ability to manipulate lightweight materials, which she initially used for fashion design and entertainment.

Short in stature, Parian wears a Victorian-style porcelain doll costume with golden curls, later changing to black after joining the Undersiders. Beneath the mask, she has dark skin, full lips, and large, dark eyes.

Non-violent by nature, Parian is socially conscious and feels a strong sense of responsibility towards those under her protection. After Leviathan's attack, she reluctantly took up a more active role, defending her territory, Dolltown.

Following the Slaughterhouse Nine's alteration of her charges, Parian accepted Skitter's offer to join the Undersiders to afford medical treatment for her people. She struggled with the transition to a more villainous role but found support in her friend and eventual lover, Flechette.

Parian grapples with the increasing pressure to fight and protect those she cares about, her power and resolve growing alongside the escalating conflicts in Brockton Bay.]

["I don't really feel guilty about the things I've done. I don't usually think about it."

Alec, born Jean-Paul Vasil and known as Regent, is the son of the notorious villain Heartbreaker and a member of the Undersiders. Triggered by his father's abuse at age ten, Alec gained the power to cause involuntary movements in others, eventually leading to complete bodily control with prolonged use.

With a pretty face, curly black hair, and a preference for expensive white clothing, Alec is described as more attractive than handsome. His costume features a white mask, a silver coronet, and a scepter that conceals a taser.

Shaped by his upbringing, Alec is amoral, passive-aggressive, and hedonistic. Despite his apparent lack of concern, he does care for his teammates, particularly Aisha. His power grants him resistance to emotion-manipulating Masters, a result of his father's influence.

Regent contributes to the Undersiders' success with his power and perceptiveness. He plays a crucial role in unmasking Shadow Stalker and participates in various conflicts alongside his team.

Tragically, Alec sacrifices himself during the battle against Behemoth in New Delhi, stepping into the Endbringer's line of fire to save Imp. His death deeply affects the Undersiders, cementing his place as a complex and ultimately loyal teammate.]

[Nikos Vasil, known as Heartbreaker, is an infamous supervillain based in Montreal. With the ability to manipulate the emotions of anyone within his line of sight, Heartbreaker has formed a cult-like harem of women who serve him zealously.

A tall, lanky man with long black hair and a scruffy beard, Heartbreaker often goes shirtless, exuding confidence and sexuality. He appears to be in his thirties or forties.

Incredibly cruel and narcissistic, Heartbreaker treats the people around him like property, collecting and disposing of women at his whims. He purposely induces trigger events in his children to bolster his forces, subjecting them to emotional abuse to keep them under control.

Heartbreaker's influence is felt through his children, particularly Regent and Cherish. His reputation as a fearsome emotional manipulator makes him a constant threat, even as he remains elusive to the authorities.

Heartbreaker's ultimate fate is not revealed, but his legacy lives on through the trauma and powers he inflicted upon his children, shaping their lives and the events of Earth Bet in many ways.]

[The Heartbroken, formerly led by the notorious supervillain Heartbreaker, are a group of his children who have inherited various emotion-manipulating powers. Raised in an environment that was a toxic mix of an extended family and a cult, the Heartbroken were subjected to their father's whims and abuse.

Under Heartbreaker's leadership, the family operated out of Montreal, constantly moving to evade authorities. The children were tasked with gathering information, fighting when necessary, and even retrieving wayward siblings like Jean-Paul and Cherie.

Despite their different mothers, the Vasil children share a similar appearance, being slender, attractive, and mostly dark-haired. Their powers, ranging from emotional manipulation to sensory deprivation, make them a formidable and unpredictable group.

The Heartbroken's influence is felt through the actions of Regent and Cherish, two of Heartbreaker's children who left the family. The PRT's response to the group highlights the difficulty in dealing with a villain who surrounds himself with brainwashed innocents and uses his own children as soldiers.

Following Heartbreaker's death at the hands of Imp, the Heartbroken come under her leadership, their role setting the stage for future developments.]

["Because I did what I had to do, I helped you, and I still feel like the stupid, self-obsessed little child that let her big brother die. It wasn't conscious, but maybe I felt like I needed to up the stakes. Pull something dramatic. Show that, with these crazy smart capes like Alexandria and Faultline around, I could still be the smartest person in the room."

Lisa Wilbourn, known as Tattletale, is a member of the Undersiders with the power to extrapolate a wealth of information from the smallest detail. Triggered after realizing she failed to prevent her brother's suicide, Lisa ran away from home and began using her power for personal gain, eventually joining the Undersiders.

In civilian guise, Lisa has dark blonde hair, green eyes, and freckles. As Tattletale, she wears a skintight black-and-lavender costume with a stylized "Tt" on the chest and a black domino mask.

Intelligent and perceptive, Lisa is known for her arrogance and abrasive personality. Despite this, she genuinely cares for her teammates, particularly Taylor, whom she actively recruited to the Undersiders.

Tattletale serves as the Undersiders' strategist and information gatherer, using her power to outmaneuver rivals and uncover secrets. Her abilities prove crucial in conflicts against Coil, the Slaughterhouse Nine, and the Endbringers. As the story progresses, Lisa's power and influence grow, cementing her role as a key player in the events that shape Earth Bet.]

[“I told you to leave my stuff alone. You said you’d respect any rules or requests if we had any, and I said to leave the ‘family’ folder alone. But you went in there?”

Aiden Tate, a young boy orphaned by the Slaughterhouse Nine, was taken in by Taylor Hebert and cared for by Charlotte. After having nightmares about space whales, Aiden drew a picture that would later prove crucial in the fight against Scion.

Small and young, with red-brown hair, Aiden is described as a quiet and solemn boy who worries a lot. His trigger event, likely a bud from Taylor's shard, grants him the ability to see through birds' eyes and control their movements.

Aiden remains a background character, but his presence and powers hint at the larger role he will play in the future. His drawing of the space whales, created after a prophetic dream, helps Tattletale make a critical realization during Gold Morning.

After the timeskip, Aiden is taken under Tattletale's wing, learning from her and the other Undersiders. His powers have grown, allowing him to control entire flocks of birds. As a young parahuman with a connection to Taylor, Aiden represents the next generation of capes, his story just beginning.]

[The Ruby Dreams Casino, located just outside the city limits of Brockton Bay, was the target of a daring heist by the Undersiders approximately five weeks before their high-profile bank robbery. Despite popular belief, the casino is not associated with or controlled by the ABB or the notorious villain Lung.

The Undersiders' successful robbery of the Ruby Dreams Casino marked a significant escalation in their criminal activities, as they had previously managed to stay under the radar of the city's hero teams. This heist, along with their subsequent bank robbery, brought the group to the attention of the authorities and solidified their reputation as a growing threat in Brockton Bay's criminal underworld.

While details of the Ruby Dreams Casino heist remain scarce, it is clear that the Undersiders' success in this endeavor emboldened them to take on even more ambitious targets, setting the stage for their future confrontations with the city's heroes and rival villain groups.]

[The Battle at the Bank was a pivotal confrontation between the Undersiders and the Brockton Bay Wards on April 14, 2011, marking a significant escalation in the Undersiders' criminal activities. During the robbery of the Brockton Bay Central Bank, the Undersiders successfully outmaneuvered the Wards, despite the unexpected presence of Panacea and Glory Girl.

Skitter's bug powers, along with the coordinated efforts of her teammates, allowed the Undersiders to neutralize the majority of the Wards. Tattletale's reveal of Panacea's past and her ability to seemingly read minds added a layer of psychological warfare to the battle.

Despite the Undersiders' victory and escape with the stolen money, the aftermath of the battle had far-reaching consequences. The Wards faced reprimands and disciplinary action, while Panacea's mental state was further strained by the confrontation. Unbeknownst to the Undersiders, their mysterious employer, Coil, had used the bank robbery as a distraction to kidnap Dinah Alcott, setting the stage for future conflicts in Brockton Bay.]

[The Battle at the Gallery was a daring attack on May 5th, 2011, by the Undersiders on a fundraiser attended by the mayor and the Brockton Bay Protectorate. Occurring shortly after the defeat of the ABB, the Undersiders aimed to embarrass the heroes and disrupt the narrative of their role in pacifying the city.

Catching the heroes off guard, the Undersiders initially disabled several PRT agents and heroes using Grue's darkness and stolen containment foam. However, the tide turned when Armsmaster captured Tattletale and engaged the rest of the team.

Through a combination of clever tactics and their powers, the Undersiders managed to incapacitate Miss Militia, Velocity, and Armsmaster. Skitter played a crucial role, using her bugs to disable Armsmaster's halberd and allowing her teammates to escape. As a final act of defiance, she left a message in bugs before fleeing the scene.

The aftermath saw the Undersiders pursued by Armsmaster and the newly arrived Dauntless, only to be thwarted by allies from Coil's organization. The battle served to further establish the Undersiders as a formidable force in Brockton Bay's underworld and set the stage for future conflicts with the city's heroes.]

[The Battle against Leviathan was a devastating conflict that took place in Brockton Bay on May 15, 2011, as the Endbringer attacked the city's vulnerable aquifer. Despite advance warning from Armsmaster's prediction software, the defending capes suffered heavy casualties as they fought to protect the city and its inhabitants.

Throughout the battle, Leviathan showcased his immense strength, speed, and durability, easily withstanding attacks from some of the most powerful capes, including Alexandria, Legend, and Dragon. The defenders, organized into groups based on their abilities, struggled to slow the Endbringer's advance, with each tidal wave he summoned claiming more lives.

Notable moments included Miss Militia's use of Bakuda's leftover bombs, temporarily trapping Leviathan, and Clockblocker's crucial intervention, freezing the Endbringer in time. Armsmaster's one-on-one duel with Leviathan, aided by his predictive software and nano-thorn halberd, ended in defeat as his weapon became lodged in the Endbringer's claw.

The battle reached a turning point when Scion arrived, forcing an injured Leviathan to retreat. In the aftermath, a memorial was erected on Captain's Hill to honor the fallen capes, with Bitch carving the names of her deceased dogs alongside the other casualties. The Battle against Leviathan left an indelible mark on Brockton Bay and its defenders, forever changing the city and its inhabitants.]

[The Brockton Bay PRT Headquarters, located in the downtown area near Arcadia High School, served as the base of operations for the local Protectorate and Wards teams. The multi-story building featured a distinctive exterior of reflective windows, with a shield logo bearing the letters "P.R.T." as its only distinguishing mark.

Inside, the headquarters housed various facilities, including a lobby with portraits of the Wards, a gift shop, interrogation rooms, an armory, and a training area. The Wards' base, a large underground domed area with adjustable walls, was accessible via a tinker-made elevator requiring retinal scans.

The building also featured a helipad on the roof, a parking garage for PRT vehicles, and a small attached hospital for discreet treatment of injured heroes. Advanced security measures were in place, such as parahuman containment cells, a hidden generator, and Dragon-maintained computers with satellite links and internal batteries.

The PRT ENE Headquarters faced numerous challenges, including damage from the Leviathan attack, assaults by the Undersiders and Travellers, and the aftermath of Shatterbird's citywide glass-shattering scream. Despite these setbacks, it remained a central hub for the city's hero teams and their efforts to maintain order in Brockton Bay.]

[The Behemoth vs. New Delhi battle on July 26th, 2011, marked a pivotal moment in the fight against the Endbringers, as the heroes faced off against the monstrous Behemoth in India's capital. With the highest attendance of any Endbringer battle, capes from around the world, including the Protectorate, Guild, Yàngbǎn, and Thanda, converged on the city to defend it.

Weaver, wearing a repainted version of her Skitter costume, joined the Chicago Wards in the fight, witnessing the destruction wrought by Behemoth firsthand. The battle saw the loss of several notable capes, including Accord and Regent, while others like Chevalier and Tattletale were severely injured.

Despite the heroes' coordinated efforts, such as Weaver and the Chicago Wards' construction of a giant lightning rod and the Undersiders' use of Foil's power to sever Behemoth's leg, the Endbringer remained a formidable foe. Phir Se's devastating time bomb attack, combined with Eidolon's defense, marked a turning point in the battle.

Ultimately, it was Scion's arrival that sealed Behemoth's fate, as the golden man delivered the killing blow. The aftermath of the battle saw a shift in the Endbringers' tactics and the emergence of new threats in the form of Khonsu and the Twins.]

[Gold Morning, the catastrophic event prophesied as the End of the World, began when Jack Slash convinced Scion to abandon his heroic pursuits and embark on a path of destruction. Over the course of four days (20 - 24th June 2013), Scion's rampage claimed the lives of billions across multiple Earths, starting with the obliteration of Great Britain and the Eastern Seaboard of the United States and Canada.

As Scion continued his attacks, targeting adults in Africa and trapping people in Russia, parahuman forces organized to evacuate civilians and mount a defense. Key meetings, reminiscent of the Khonsu Meeting, brought together various factions to share information and strategize.

The first major battle, the oil-rig battle, resulted in devastating losses, with roughly half of Earth Bet's population perishing. Scion discovered and destroyed the Cauldron Compound, ending the life of his comatose partner.

In the final confrontation, thousands of capes united under Khepri's command to defeat Scion, shattering landmasses on multiple worlds in the process. Parahumans who fought in Gold Morning now wear a distinctive yellow insignia to commemorate their participation in this world-altering event.]

["You know how it is. You find your niche, you stay in your niche, you stay comfortable."

Über, a supervillain from Brockton Bay, formed a videogame-themed criminal duo with his partner, Leet. Tall and muscular, Über's power grants him a high level of skill in any specific technique he focuses on, though he lacks the broader knowledge and fundamentals of those skills.

Despite his potential, Über's loyalty to Leet held him back, as the pair gained notoriety for their incompetence and despicable behavior, such as beating prostitutes for online views. They often wore costumes based on the videogames they themed their crimes around.

 Über and Leet clashed with the Undersiders, were contracted by Coil, and were briefly captured by Echidna. After the Echidna incident, the duo, along with Circus, left Brockton Bay for South America. However, Leet's death and Über's subsequent legal troubles led to his arrest and imprisonment.

Über serves as an example of wasted potential, a villain with a powerful ability held back by his own choices and associations. His arc highlights the consequences of remaining in one's comfort zone and the ultimate price of loyalty to the wrong person.]

["They're laughing at you, Leet. You're trying to be all dramatic, all intense for your viewers, and they're just sitting at their computers, snorting over how much you suck."

Leet, a scrawny and unpleasant supervillain from Brockton Bay, formed a videogame-themed criminal duo with his partner, Über. As a Free Tinker, Leet could theoretically create anything, but his power came with severe drawbacks: he could only make something once, and the more similar a creation was to a previous one, the higher the chances of a spectacular failure.

Despicable and annoying, Leet owned deliberately shocking t-shirts and had no qualms about beating prostitutes for online views. His costumes, like Über's, were usually based on video game themes.

Leet and Über clashed with the Undersiders, were contracted by Coil, and were briefly captured by Echidna. After the Echidna incident, the duo, along with Circus, left Brockton Bay for South America, where Leet was eventually killed after crossing the wrong people.

Leet's serves as a cautionary tale of wasted potential and the consequences of not understanding one's powers. His unsatisfied Shard actively sabotaged him, leading to his failures and ultimate demise. Despite his versatile ability, Leet's poor choices and lack of growth led to his downfall.]

[The Red Hand, also known as Red Handed or the Red Hands, is a villainous group of professional thieves allied with the Undersiders. Known for their distinctive red gloves and preference for avoiding direct confrontation, the group initially posed a potential threat to Brockton Bay but eventually formed a non-aggression pact and alliance with the Undersiders.

The group's leader, Rook, was killed during Scion's rampage, leaving Cozen, his second-in-command, to take over leadership. Cozen, a young woman with old-fashioned clothes and a mask around her eyes, possesses the ability to create pocket dimensions linked to specific locations, allowing her to store and retrieve objects and people.

Other notable members include Getaway, who can teleport to pre-set areas, and Rifle, who can turn any projectile into one with enhanced range and perception. Getaway wears a cowl with a peaked hood, while Rifle dresses like a special ops agent with a complicated night-vision mount.

The Red Hand's alliance with the Undersiders proved beneficial, as Tattletale trusted them enough to hire the group for a job stealing PRT files. However, following the deaths of Grue and Rook and the destruction of Brockton Bay, the Red Hand split away from the Undersiders.]

[The Teeth are an itinerant villain group known for their ethos of violence, anarchy, and profit at any cost. Originally operating in Brockton Bay, they later established cells in Boston and New York. The group moves between cities frequently, looting and harassing before relocating. Their costumes feature blades, spikes, and macabre elements like teeth and bones, making it difficult to distinguish between powered and unpowered members.

The Teeth are led by the Butcher, a title passed down through the murder of the previous leader. Butcher XIV, formerly known as Quarrel, possesses the powers and consciousnesses of her predecessors. Other notable members include Animos, who can transform into a power-nullifying creature; Hemorrhagia, with limited blood control and biokinesis; Reaver; Spree, capable of rapidly producing short-lived clones; and Vex, who can create razor-sharp forcefields.

After nearly being wiped out by the Slaughterhouse Nine, the Teeth returned to Brockton Bay to challenge the Undersiders. Despite their aggressive tactics, they were ultimately defeated, with Butcher XIV killed by a remnant of Cherish's power. However, the group remained a potential threat, highlighting their resilience and the difficulties in coordinating a response against their mobile operations.]

[Downtown Brockton Bay, the central area of the city, is characterized by its wide streets, sidewalks, and a mix of old and new buildings, including skyscrapers. The south-east part of downtown is primarily housing, with some gang tags and broken windows. Lord Street, the main road running through the city, traces the line of the bay.

Several notable locations are found downtown, including Arcadia High, the PRT ENE Headquarters, Tattletale's headquarters, the Towers, Brockton Bay Central Library, and the Medhall Corporation building. The area is also home to Palanquin, a nightclub, and the Forsberg Gallery.

Following Leviathan's attack, downtown was significantly damaged, with Crater Lake forming in the center. The Scar, created by the PRT using Bakuda's bombs against the Slaughterhouse Nine, further scarred the landscape.

Various factions vied for control of downtown with the Empire Eighty-Eight, Coil, the Travelers, and later the Undersiders all claiming territory at different points. The portal to Earth Gimel, created during the Echidna incident, was also located downtown. Despite the damage and reconstruction efforts, downtown remained a crucial hub of activity in Brockton Bay.]

[The Docks, located in the north and east of Brockton Bay, is an area characterized by urban decay and failing infrastructure. Despite its name, much of the Docks are situated away from the water, with abandoned factories, warehouses, and garages dominating the landscape. The south end of the Docks borders Downtown, while the southwest end features residential areas, schools, small businesses, and restaurants.

The Docks are known for their cramped tenements, where multiple families share basic amenities, and the area has a reputation for harboring criminals and gang members. Ironically, the buildings in the Docks survived the Battle against Leviathan relatively unscathed, although the water and power infrastructure was severely damaged.

Notable locations within the Docks include the Trainyard, situated opposite the Boardwalk, which contains abandoned boxcars and a rarely-used train station. The Undersiders' base, located in an abandoned Redmond Welding factory building, is also found in the Docks, along with Bitch's improvised dog shelter. Coil, as part of his plan to control the city, bought out numerous properties in the area.

Other points of interest include the homes of Taylor and Danny Hebert on the periphery of the Docks, and Chariot's brick tenement building.]

[The Protectorate ENE Headquarters, commonly known as the PHQ, is a refitted oil rig located off the coast of Brockton Bay. Serving as the base of operations for the Brockton Bay Protectorate, the PHQ is a marvel of architectural design, featuring arches, spires, and sweeping lines, all lit by tinted spotlights.

The PHQ is protected by a forcefield bubble that gives everything seen through it an oversaturated appearance, as well as a missile defense system. A forcefield roadway connects the base to the mainland, allowing for easy access to and from the city.

Visible from nearly any point on the Docks and the Boardwalk, the PHQ stands as a symbol of the Protectorate's presence and power in Brockton Bay. Despite its impressive defenses, the base had never had cause to use its forcefield or missile turrets prior to the Battle against Leviathan.

During the Endbringer's attack, the PHQ was ripped from its location and flung against the shore, suffering significant damage. In the years following, the remains of the PHQ were repurposed, with its forcefield being used to block some of the waves created by Scion's attack on Brockton Bay during Gold Morning.]

[The Scar, a large swath of destruction located in central Downtown Brockton Bay, was created when PRT Director Emily Piggot ordered several of Bakuda's bombs to be dropped on the Slaughterhouse Nine. Spanning three blocks in width, the Scar is filled with lingering, dangerous effects from the bombs, including low radioactive fallout, eternally burning fires, a cloud of hazardous white vapor, and a patch of pale, spreading earth.

Within the Scar, sections of the landscape have been transmuted into various materials, some rare and valuable like gold and diamond veins. Unexploded bombs remain scattered throughout the area, posing an ongoing threat. The silicon statues of Mannequin and Crawler, two members of the Slaughterhouse Nine killed during the bombing, stand as eerie reminders of the destruction.

Initially open to the public, the Scar was later enclosed by a windowless, blocky structure to prevent the bombs' effects from spreading and harming civilians. During the timeskip, treasure seekers attempting to exploit the Scar's transmutational effects fell victim to an undetonated bomb, becoming trapped in a bubble of frozen time.

When Scion shattered Brockton Bay during Gold Morning, the Scar's contents were released, forcing capes and rescue crews to work on containing the dangerous fallout.]

[The Brockton Bay Portal, an interdimensional gateway connecting Earth Bet to Earth Gimel, was created through the combined powers of Labyrinth and Scrub during the Battle against Echidna. Located in Downtown Brockton Bay, the portal appears as a tower with a small area of ground beneath it, perceivable only by its edges.

Surrounding the portal is a solid white, windowless building designed by Accord and constructed and owned by Tattletale's organization. The tower, taller than the nearby skyscrapers, is encircled by numerous ramps leading into the building at different heights, resembling flower petals. A system of train tracks extends from the base of the tower in every direction, while adjoining buildings serve as administration and defense for the portal.

The portal's creation sparked national debate over property rights and became a focal point for the Undersiders' influence in Brockton Bay. During Gold Morning, Scion's attack destroyed the Earth Bet side of the tower, shattering the land beneath it, while the Earth Gimel side remained intact. The Brockton Bay Portal stands as a symbol of the changing landscape and the growing connections between alternate Earths.]

[The Endbringer Fight Memorial, erected five days after Leviathan's attack on Brockton Bay, stands as a tribute to the capes who lost their lives during the battle. Located on Captain's Hill, at the base of the mountains west of the city, the memorial is an obelisk made of black marble with stainless steel lettering.

The monument's base and corners are left unpolished and rough, while its four sides are smoothed and polished. Etched into the obelisk are the names of fallen capes and civilians, although some civilian names are omitted for privacy reasons. Notable capes memorialized include Aegis, Dauntless, Fenja, Gallant, Kaiser, Manpower, Shielder, and Velocity.

In a poignant addition, Bitch carved the names of her eight dogs who perished during the attack - KOOROW, BULLIT, MILK, STUMPY, BROOTUS, JOODUS, AXIL, and GINGIR - underneath the list of names on the final side of the memorial.

The Endbringer Fight Memorial serves as a somber reminder of the sacrifices made by heroes and villains alike in the face of an overwhelming threat, and the toll that Endbringer battles take on the cape community and the city as a whole.]

[Arcadia High, located near Downtown Brockton Bay and Brockton Bay Central, is a four-story public school known for its exceptional educational standards and its status as a vocational school. The school's layout consists of two long buildings connected by a shorter crosspiece, forming an 'H' shape. The south side houses classrooms, the cafeteria, and the gym, while the north side features an auditorium and additional classrooms.

Most of the Brockton Bay Wards attend Arcadia High, as it allows them to spend half of their school day working as superheroes. The school's proximity to the middle school attended by Dinah Alcott also plays a role in the story's events.

Arcadia High is equipped with a Faraday cage to block students from using cellphones during class hours. The main office and administrative facilities are located in the center of the school, with emergency exits leading to an open space surrounded by walls lined with windows. The school's design and security measures contribute to the challenges faced by characters navigating its premises during critical moments.]

[Immaculata High, informally known as the "rich kid's school," is a Christian private school located in the south end of Brockton Bay, south-west of The Towers in the city's nicest area. The school's location and religious affiliation set it apart from other educational institutions in the city.

Several Immaculata students, including Park Jihoo, were among those kidnapped and implanted with bombs by the villain Bakuda. Tragically, Park Jihoo was killed for refusing to attack the Undersiders, highlighting the brutal nature of the conflict between the city's villains and the innocent civilians caught in the crossfire.

Despite the challenges faced by Brockton Bay, including Leviathan's attack and the Slaughterhouse Nine's rampage, Immaculata High managed to survive and continue operating. In the aftermath of these events, students wearing Immaculata uniforms could be seen commuting to and from the school, a testament to the resilience of the city's inhabitants and the enduring presence of the institution in the face of adversity,]

[Winslow High, a public high school located in Brockton Bay, played a significant role in the life of Taylor Hebert, the protagonist of Worm. The school was known for its poor management, gang activity, and a pervasive bullying problem, exemplified by the actions of "The Trio" - Sophia Hess, Emma Barnes, and Madison Clements - who targeted Taylor for an extended period.

Notable students at Winslow included Taylor Hebert, Sophia Hess (Shadow Stalker), and Greg Veder, while key faculty members were Mr. Gladly, Mrs. Knott, and Mr. Quinlan. The school's lockers were separate from the doors, requiring padlocks, and the third-floor girls' bathroom had stalls that opened outwards.

After the Leviathan attack, many students evacuated, and Sophia Hess was expelled due to Regent's interference. Following the Echidna incident, Winslow closed, with remaining students transferred to Arcadia High. The new vice-principal, in contact with Tattletale, punished Emma Barnes for her bullying and gave Taylor special treatment.

During Gold Morning, Scion's attack on Brockton Bay destroyed Winslow High, erasing the physical remnants of Taylor's painful memories, but not the impact the school had on her life and the shaping of her identity as a cape.]

[The Boat Graveyard, also known as the Lord's Port, is a section of Brockton Bay's coastline located north of the Market and about a forty-minute walk from the Downtown portal. Originally an upper section of the Docks, the Boat Graveyard became a dumping ground for abandoned and sunken ships following the collapse of the local industry. Protesters deliberately sank a container ship and trapped other boats in the harbor, making it difficult for authorities to clear the area.

After Leviathan's attack, the Boat Graveyard's ships were slammed into the coastline, causing extensive damage and spreading rusted metal across the area. Notable landmarks include an unstable arch formed by two ships and a beached boat where Cherish, a member of the Slaughterhouse Nine, was temporarily imprisoned by Coil's Organization.

The Undersiders attempted to retrieve Cherish but were met with decoys and a note acknowledging defeat. Cherish was later moved further into the Bay to prevent her uncontrolled powers from harming others. Post-Echidna, Danny Hebert began efforts to clean up the Boat Graveyard.

During Gold Morning, the Boat Graveyard was completely destroyed when Scion sank Brockton Bay. In Earth Gimel, Charlotte and Brooks stayed in a cottage overlooking the location where the Graveyard would have been.]

[Fugly Bob's, a fast-food restaurant located on the edge of Brockton Bay's Lord Street Market, is known for its greasy, oversized burgers and casual atmosphere. The part-restaurant, part-bar, part-shack establishment overlooks the beach and is a popular spot for locals, despite the unhealthy nature of its menu.

The restaurant's signature dish is the Fugly Bob Challenger, a burger so large that customers who manage to finish it don't have to pay for their meal. Other notable menu items include the Hideous Bob (Fugly Bob's take on a Big Mac), bacon cheeseburgers, and a portobello-beef double-decker burger. The restaurant also offers a variety of sides, such as fries, sweet potato fries, onion rings, and deep-fried zucchini, as well as desserts and beer.
