The Undersiders (minus Rachel) visit Fugly Bob's in their civilian identities the day after the bank robbery, using the restaurant's outdoor seating area to discuss their plans while maintaining a degree of privacy.

During Gold Morning, Fugly Bob's is destroyed by Scion as collateral damage during his attack on the Eastern coast of the United States, marking the end of the iconic Brockton Bay establishment.]

[The Lord Street Market, commonly known as "the Market," is an open-air market located in the north end of Brockton Bay, past the Boardwalk and south of the Boat Graveyard. The Market is situated on an expanse of asphalt surrounded by tall grass, with stalls that can be rented by anyone for $50 to $300, depending on the day of the week.

Vendors at the Market sell a wide variety of items, including handicrafts, overstock from Boardwalk shops, ice cream, puppies, cape merchandise, clothing, books, and food. The Market serves as an alternative to garage sales for residents of the north end and is considered a shopping destination comparable to a mall.

Notable landmarks near the Market include Fugly Bob's, a well-known burger joint located on the edge of the Market overlooking the beach. The same enforcers who operate on the Boardwalk help keep the Market crime-free.

The Heberts consider trips to the Market as family outings, and the Undersiders pass through the area while deciding on their next move after the bank robbery. The Market is also used as a cover story for Taylor's injuries from Bakuda's pain bomb. Following the Battle against Leviathan, the Market is closed for a time, even after the debris is cleared.]

[Somer's Rock, a family-owned pub in Brockton Bay, serves as a neutral meeting ground for the city's various villain groups. Located on a street filled with hole-in-the-wall businesses, the pub's exterior is nondescript, with peeling gray-white paint and rust-stained iron bars on the windows.

Inside, Somer's Rock is described as "dim, dingy, and depressing," with a wood floor stained the same color as the counter and dark green curtains and tablecloths. The only sources of brightness are the yellow lights cast by old light bulbs.

The pub is staffed by twin brother bartenders and a teenage daughter, with at least one of the servers being deaf. Somer's Rock plays a crucial role in the story when the Empire Eighty-Eight, Undersiders, Faultline's Crew, and the Merchants gather there to discuss their response to the Azn Bad Boys' actions following Bakuda's bombing spree.

As a neutral territory, Somer's Rock provides a unique setting where the usually antagonistic villain groups can come together to negotiate and form temporary alliances, highlighting the complex dynamics of Brockton Bay's criminal underworld.]

[The Medhall Corporation, a pharmaceutical company headquartered in Brockton Bay, serves as a front for the Empire Eighty-Eight's illegal activities. With a logo featuring a crown on a red-and-yellow background, Medhall presents itself as a legitimate business while secretly laundering money and employing many of the gang's members.

Max Anders, the President and CEO of Medhall, uses his position to facilitate the Empire's operations and provide a steady income for its members. The company's headquarters, located in the downtown area of Brockton Bay, becomes a target for mercenaries following the capture of the rival gang leaders Lung and Bakuda.

After Coil publicly reveals the identities of the Empire's parahuman members, Medhall's assets are frozen pending a government investigation. The company's fate remains uncertain following Max Anders' death, with his son Theo potentially inheriting some of the remaining assets.

Medhall's role highlights the intricate web of connections between legitimate businesses and criminal organizations in Brockton Bay, as well as the challenges faced by authorities in untangling these relationships and bringing those responsible to justice.]

[The Towers, a residential district located in the heart of Downtown Brockton Bay, is considered one of the nicer parts of the city. Built upon a series of distinct hills, the Towers are situated southwest of the New Wave residences and Immaculata High.

Notable residents of the Towers include Theo Anders, Gallant, Rune, and Dauntless, as well as the Parahumans Online user White Fairy, who would meet with local residents to confirm their "At Ground Zero: Brockton Bay" user badges and provide supplies if needed.

Following the Battle against Leviathan, the Towers remained relatively unscathed compared to other areas of the city. Trickster, a member of Coil's Organization, claimed the area as his territory and drove out looters to maintain control.

At some point, the Towers became the site of a massacre that claimed the lives of several Merchants, highlighting the ongoing power struggles and violence within Brockton Bay's criminal underworld.

The Towers serve as a contrast to the more run-down areas of the city, showcasing the stark divide between the wealthy and the less fortunate in Brockton Bay, while also demonstrating the far-reaching impact of parahuman conflicts on the city's residents.]

[New York, one of the most competitive areas for capes and gangs in the United States, is known for its focus on destructive might in cape culture. The city has close connections with Boston and Brockton Bay, with multiple individuals and groups operating across all three cities.

The New York PRT Department is one of the top departments in the country, focusing on overall administration and decision-making for director placements, department prioritization, and crisis response. The New York Protectorate and Wards constitute the largest cape groups in the United States, with notable members including Legend, Chevalier, and Prism.

Villainous organizations in New York include the Adepts, a group of self-professed magic users; the Elite, with one of the least violent and most professional cells; and the Teeth, a gang that also operates in Boston and previously in Brockton Bay.

New York is attacked by Behemoth in 1994, targeted by the Slaughterhouse Nine-Thousand, and partially destroyed during Scion's rampage. The city serves as the final staging ground in the battle against Scion and is rebuilt after his defeat, with portals connecting New York to other worlds.]

[an Francisco, home to PRT Department 13, is a healthy city with a highly competitive cape environment. The PRT heroes maintain control over the city's above-board activities, while the Elite, a villain organization that originated in San Francisco as "Uppermost," manages the city's criminal elements. The two groups are engaged in a long-term shadow battle for dominance, constantly vying for influence and resources while carefully avoiding public confrontations.

The city is also home to the head office of Watchdog, a PRT-affiliated organization focused on preventing economic and political disruption by parahumans. Watchdog employs think tanks of Thinkers to analyze large quantities of data and regularly launches investigations within the PRT.

Several corporate hero teams, such as Eminent, operate in the Bay Area, contributing to the city's competitive atmosphere. San Francisco has been the target of at least one attack by the Endbringer Leviathan, which is implied to have sunk the sub-city of Emeryville.

The delicate balance of power between the PRT and the Elite, along with the high standards for showmanship and style among capes, makes San Francisco a unique and challenging environment for both heroes and villains alike.]

[The Elite, the largest villain organization and second-largest parahuman organization in the United States, originated in San Francisco as "Uppermost," a group of rogues involved in production and entertainment. After the passage of the NEPEA-5 bill, which targeted parahuman involvement in business and media, Uppermost disbanded, with many members joining the Protectorate or Wards. However, the core group reorganized as the Elite, quickly expanding their influence.

The Elite operates through a loose pyramid structure of cells, with the top cell in San Francisco managing national interests. They seize control of areas through economic and political means, using sabotage, organized crime connections, and swift strikes to undermine local opposition. Rogues are folded into the organization, while villains are forced to be beholden to the Elite. The group also controls numerous corporate hero teams behind the scenes.

The Elite maintains a presence across the western seaboard, including California, Nevada, Arizona, Washington, Idaho, Oregon, and Florida, with tentative holds in New York and various cape cities. During Gold Morning, the Elite attended the meeting at Cauldron's headquarters but chose to focus on building a new society rather than participating in the fight against Scion. As a result, the Undersiders set Leviathan upon them, leading to the demise of several prominent members and presumably the organization's downfall.]

[Earth Bet, the primary setting of Worm, is an alternate version of Earth that diverged from Earth Aleph around 1982 with the arrival of the entity known as Scion. The emergence of parahumans and their impact on society has shaped Earth Bet's history, leading to the formation of various superhero and villain organizations.

Notable residents of Earth Bet include the Undersiders, a group of teenage supervillains; Cauldron, a secretive organization dedicated to saving humanity from Scion; the Protectorate and the Wards, government-sponsored hero teams; and the Endbringers, monstrous beings that periodically attack cities across the globe.

Earth Bet is home to numerous countries and regions of interest, such as the United States, Canada, the Chinese Union-Imperial, Japan, India, Russia, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Australia, and Antarctica. Each area has its own unique parahuman culture and organizations, such as the Elite in the United States and the Suits in China.

Earth Bet faces numerous challenges and catastrophic events, including the Endbringer attacks, the Slaughterhouse Nine's rampages, and ultimately, Scion's betrayal and the resulting apocalyptic battle known as Gold Morning.]

[Earth Aleph, a parallel world to Earth Bet, diverged from its counterpart around 1982 with the appearance of Scion. It is the home reality of the Travelers, a group of teenage parahuman nomads who were later transported to Earth Bet by the Simurgh.

Earth Aleph bears a closer resemblance to our own world than Earth Bet, with fewer and less powerful parahumans. Individuals born before the divergence point have counterparts on both Earths, while those born after do not.

Despite its relative normalcy, Earth Aleph is still affected by the presence of parahumans and the occasional incursion from other realities. The world serves as a source of stability and a potential refuge for those seeking to escape the chaos and conflicts of Earth Bet.

Following the cataclysmic event known as Gold Morning, Earth Aleph was sealed off from the rest of the multiverse to protect its inhabitants. Taylor Hebert was depowered and exiled to Earth Aleph alongside her father by Contessa, serving as a bittersweet conclusion to her journey and a new beginning in a world free from the influence of entities and parahuman conflicts.]

[Earth Gimel is an alternate Earth that diverged from other human-occupied Earths approximately 5,000 years ago. It became a refuge for survivors during the cataclysmic event known as Gold Morning and later served as a new home for millions of refugees from Earth Bet.

The majority of Gimel's population resides in the sprawling megalopolis known as the City, which formed around the portals connecting Gimel to Bet. Despite the relative safety and support provided by the City, many challenges arise, including limited resources, political struggles, and the constant influx of refugees.

Notable residents of Earth Gimel include the heroic team Breakthrough, the Wardens, various other hero and villain groups, and the interdimensional settlers and refugees who now call the world home. Key locations include the City, Nilles University, Hollow Point, New Brockton, and New York Central.

Earth Gimel faces numerous trials, such as the aftermath of the Mathers Compound Assault, conflicts with Earth Cheit, and the devastating impact of the Titans. Despite these hardships, the inhabitants of Gimel continue to rebuild and adapt, striving to create a new society in the wake of the multiverse-shattering events that brought them together.]

[Earth Nun, also known as Earth N, is one of the "corner worlds" that was colonized shortly after the events of Gold Morning. With a population of approximately 150,000 people, 90% of whom live within 25 miles of the primary portal to Earth Gimel, Earth Nun is a sparsely populated world divided into a dozen isolated settlements.

The construction and resources on Earth Nun are generally inferior to those found on Earth Gimel, with buildings often made from basic materials such as plywood, corrugated steel, and plastic. The world is heavily influenced by various villain groups, including those led by Lord of Loss, Marquis, Deader, and Goner.

Notable residents of Earth Nun include the aforementioned villains, as well as Barcode, Little Midas, Semiramis, and Old Man. Key locations on Earth Nun include The Lodge and Frontier Row.

Earth Nun serves as a haven for unsettled minor villains and a site of conflict between various villain factions vying for control over the world's limited resources and territory.]

[Earth Shin, also known as Supreme Earth, is an alternate reality that exists in close parallel to Earth Aleph and Earth Bet. It was discovered by Professor Haywire and heavily classified by the PRT due to the potential threat posed by its ruler, Goddess, and her mind control abilities.

In the years leading up to the events in Earth Bet, a portal to Earth Shin in White Rock, British Columbia, became public knowledge, leading to increased smuggling activity and the eventual quarantine of the area due to the spread of diseases. This portal also served as the means by which Goddess and her cluster were exiled to Earth Shin by Cauldron.

During the events of Gold Morning, Khepri briefly visited Earth Shin and seized its occupants for her war against Scion. Only Goddess and her inner circle were able to temporarily resist Khepri's control.

Earth Shin is mentioned as a potential source of resources and as a cautionary tale regarding the dangers of unchecked parahuman influence, but it does not play a significant role in relation to Earth Bet.]

[Contessa's world, a reality separate from Earth Bet, was home to Fortuna, the young girl who would later become Contessa. When the entity known as Eden crash-landed on this world, it tore a hole between dimensions, allowing Fortuna to cross over and encounter the wounded entity directly.

The limited level of technology and global interconnectedness on Contessa's world is evident in Fortuna's lack of awareness regarding the existence of people with dark skin, suggesting a more isolated and less advanced society compared to Earth Bet.

After meeting Eden and drinking a portion of the entity's body fluids, Fortuna gained her powerful ability to see the "Path to Victory." With the help of this newfound power and the guidance of the mysterious Doctor Mother, Fortuna killed Eden before the entity could recover from its injuries.

This pivotal moment set the stage for the creation of Cauldron and the organization's efforts to understand and harness the power of the entities in preparation for the final confrontation against Scion. Contessa's world, while not explored in detail, serves as a crucial starting point for one of the most influential people on Earth Bet.]

["You're a strange one, aren't you? But I can work with strange. I think we're going to get along just fine, you and I."

March, born May, is a Japanese-American villain and member of Flechette's multitrigger cluster. Driven by an unhealthy obsession with Flechette, March pursues her relentlessly, joining minor villain groups in New York that are likely to be targeted by the Wards.

As March, she wears a military-style uniform with a feathered cap and a rabbit mask, carrying a rapier as her primary weapon. Her cluster powers grant her enhanced timing and the ability to imbue objects with a weakened version of Flechette's power, allowing her to cut through nearly any defense.

Orphaned during her trigger event, March's personality underwent a drastic change, leading her down a path of villainy and obsession. She is theatrical, cunning, and utterly fixated on Flechette, going to great lengths to insert herself into the other girl's life.

March appears as a minor but persistent threat, her actions driven by her singular goal of claiming Flechette for herself. Her cluster powers and strategic mind make her a formidable foe, despite her lack of a major role in the overarching events.]

["I think she's a lot like us. She's not a villain in the pure sense of the word, but she's not a hero either. She's somewhere in between, striving for an ideal that only she understands. She's ruthless in a way that's almost admirable, if it wasn't so terrifying."

Skitter, the notorious bug-controlling villain of Brockton Bay, strikes fear into the hearts of heroes and villains alike. Clad in a black-and-grey spider silk bodysuit adorned with insect-themed armor panels, Skitter's appearance is as unsettling as her power. Her yellow-lensed mask, designed to resemble a bug's mandibles, hides her face but not her reputation.

With an almost limitless ability to control arthropods within a few city blocks, Skitter's swarms are a force to be reckoned with. She can direct her minions with precision, using them to gather information, create distractions, or launch devastating attacks. Her power grants her enhanced senses and an uncanny ability to multitask, making her a formidable opponent in any situation.

Despite her villainous status, Skitter is driven by a complex set of morals and a desire to protect her territory and those she cares about. Her ruthless tactics and unwavering determination have earned her both respect and notoriety among the cape community. To the PRT, she is a Master 8 threat, a rating that only hints at the true extent of her power and the fear she instills in those who cross her path.]

[Taylor's control over her arthropod minions is both precise and powerful, allowing her to direct their actions in ways that push the limits of their capabilities. She can command them to perform tasks that would normally be impossible or self-destructive, such as producing excessive amounts of silk or stinging with little to no venom.

The range of creatures Taylor can control is determined by her understanding of the term "bug" at the time of her trigger event. This includes most arthropods, as well as some other invertebrates like worms and certain sea creatures. However, her power has limitations, such as being unable to control creatures below a certain size or those with more complex nervous systems.

Taylor's control is not automatic; she must actively direct her minions, and once they leave her range, they revert to their normal behavior patterns. However, if she issues a command while they are still under her control, they will continue to follow that order until she consciously dismisses it or provides a new one. This level of control demonstrates the strength and versatility of Taylor's power, which she creatively exploits to overcome challenges.]

["She's not the same person she was before. The anger, the ruthlessness, it's still there, but tempered by experience and a newfound sense of purpose. She's a hero now, in the truest sense of the word, even if her methods are sometimes unconventional."

Weaver, formerly known as Skitter, has undergone a significant transformation since her days as a villain in Brockton Bay. Her costume, now a sleek silk bodysuit with white armor panels and a more heroic aesthetic, reflects her change in allegiance and mindset.

As a member of the Chicago Wards, Weaver's powers have grown, with an increased range and even greater control over her swarms. She has honed her skills in hand-to-hand combat and tactics, becoming a formidable force on the battlefield. Her creativity and adaptability shine through in her use of her powers, from creating silk barriers to forming decoys out of her bugs.

Despite her heroic status, Weaver remains a controversial figure, with many still wary of her past and her uncompromising approach to fighting crime. However, her dedication to protecting the innocent and her willingness to make hard choices have earned her the respect of her teammates and the wider cape community. Weaver represents a new chapter in Taylor's life, one marked by redemption, growth, and an unwavering commitment to doing what's right.]

["She's not even human anymore, not really. She's something else entirely, a force of nature, a goddess of control. It's terrifying, but at the same time, it's the only thing that can save us."

Khepri, the final evolution of Taylor's powers, is a being of unimaginable scope and influence. Born from Panacea's alterations to Taylor's brain, Khepri's abilities extend far beyond mere bug control. With a range of nearly sixteen feet, she can crudely control every sapient and sentient creature, including parahumans and humans, turning them into extensions of her own will.

Though her insect control is diminished in precision, Khepri's new powers more than compensate. She can sense the inner workings of those under her control, co-opt their senses, and command their powers with frightening efficiency. The cost, however, is Taylor's own humanity. As time passes, the barrier between Taylor and her shard blurs, her body and mind slowly deteriorating.

In the face of Scion's apocalyptic rampage, Khepri stands as the only hope for humanity's survival. Commanding an army of thousands of parahumans and trillions of insects across multiple Earths, she coordinates the final battle against the entity, pushing her powers to their absolute limit. Khepri represents the ultimate sacrifice, the surrender of one's very self for the greater good, and the terrifying potential of unshackled parahuman abilities.]

[One of the most remarkable aspects of Taylor's power is her ability to multitask on an unprecedented scale. She can simultaneously control countless insects, directing them to perform complex tasks while also focusing on other matters at hand. The level of control she exerts can vary from general instructions, which allow her to maintain a vague awareness of her swarm's movements, to precise guidance for individual insects, granting her a more detailed understanding of their actions and surroundings.

However, this multitasking ability is not without its limitations. Taylor can become distracted by the sensory input from her insects, especially when faced with contradictory signals, such as those from Panacea's modified bugs. It is her shard that handles the multitasking behind the scenes, allowing Taylor to independently control her swarm. Outside of her bug control, Taylor's power does not grant her enhanced multitasking abilities in other areas.

Interestingly, Taylor's power can sometimes act on its own, responding to her subconscious thoughts or habits without her explicit instruction. This can lead to unintended consequences, such as her bugs revealing her presence when she is eavesdropping or performing actions automatically when she is incapacitated or in an altered mental state.]

[Taylor's ability to offload her emotions onto her swarm is a unique aspect of her power that grants her a significant advantage in various situations. By channeling her feelings and body language through her bugs, Taylor can project an aura of unwavering calm, even in the face of extreme stress or danger. This emotional masking provides her with a degree of resistance against Thinker powers, making it difficult for even the most powerful Thinkers to accurately read her.

Notable examples of this ability in action include Taylor's confrontation with Alexandria, where she used her emotional offloading to catch the veteran hero off guard, and her interactions with Armsmaster, Cherish, and Jack Slash, all of whom struggled to get a precise read on her true feelings. This emotional camouflage can be so effective that even those closest to Taylor, such as Tattletale, sometimes have trouble understanding her.

The ability to separate her emotions from her physical presence allows Taylor to maintain a clear head and make rational decisions in high-pressure situations. It is a testament to her creativity and adaptability, as she consistently finds new ways to leverage her powers to gain an edge over her opponents, both physically and psychologically.]

[Taylor's ability to perceive the world through her bugs' senses is a crucial aspect of her power, albeit one that comes with limitations. The sensory input she receives is often described as "fuzzy" and difficult for her human mind to interpret, with only sporadic moments of clear sight and hearing. Despite practice, Taylor's ability to make sense of this input remains unreliable for much of the story.

However, Taylor's understanding of her bugs' senses does improve over time, particularly in high-stress situations that mirror the emotions of her trigger event. In these moments, her power seems to grant her enhanced clarity, allowing her to discern intricate details about her surroundings and the people within them.

By combining the sensory input from large numbers of insects, Taylor can construct a remarkably accurate mental picture of the areas her swarm interacts with. This, coupled with her innate understanding of her bugs' biology and location, grants her enhanced aim and reaction times, enabling her to dodge attacks with uncanny precision.

Despite these advantages, Taylor's sensory abilities are not infallible. In environments with few bugs or materials that her insects cannot effectively interact with, her perception of the area can become less reliable.]

[Taylor's power has a limited range, initially extending to about a tenth of a mile around her and later expanding to cover 3-4 city blocks, with each block being roughly 300 feet. However, this range is not static and can be affected by various factors.

During periods of intense stress that mirror the emotions of her trigger event, such as frustration, hopelessness, despair, or betrayal, Taylor's range can dramatically increase. In one instance, it extended to over six and a half blocks, accompanied by faster response times from her bugs and enhanced sensory clarity. These power boosts are temporary, fading as her emotional state returns to normal.

Nevertheless, Taylor's base range gradually increases over time as she engages in more conflicts and claims territory. From an initial radius of two blocks, her range expands to three blocks and eventually reaches a stable radius of five blocks, or between 900 and 1,500 feet, during her time as a warlord in Brockton Bay.

By the time she fights Behemoth in India as part of the Chicago Wards, Taylor's range has grown to a radius of 1,800 feet, or roughly six blocks, doubling her full diameter to 3,600 feet. Additionally, she experiences a temporary range boost while under the influence of The Yàngbǎn's power-magnifying field.]

["I know my daughter. She's a good person. She's not the monster you're making her out to be."

Danny Hebert is the father of Taylor Hebert and the head of hiring at the Dockworkers Association in Brockton Bay. A tall, thin, balding man with dark hair, glasses, and green eyes, Danny is known for his enormous temper, which he has learned to keep in check over the years.

Despite his love for his daughter, Danny struggles to maintain a close relationship with her following the death of his wife, Annette. He blames himself for not being there for Taylor during her most challenging times and fears that she no longer sees him as a significant part of her life.

Danny grapples with the revelation of Taylor's secret identity as the villain Skitter. Despite his initial shock and confusion, he remains a loyal and supportive father, trusting in his daughter's inherent goodness and defending her against those who would paint her as a monster. Danny's unwavering love and belief in Taylor serve as a testament to the strength of their bond, even in the face of unimaginable challenges.]

["She taught something precious to each of us."

Annette Rose Hebert, the mother of Taylor Hebert and wife of Danny Hebert, was an English Professor at a college in Brockton Bay. A tall, willowy woman with long, dark curly hair and a thin-lipped, expressive mouth, Annette was known for her gentleness, warmth, and brilliance.

In her youth, Annette was part of Lustrum's gang before it devolved into a violent mob. She met her husband, Danny, in college and had their daughter, Taylor, soon after. As an introvert, Annette shared her husband's preference for low-key outings and intellectual pursuits.

Tragically, Annette died in a car crash around a year before Taylor started high school. It was later revealed that she had been using her cell phone at the time of the collision, leading to an unofficial ban on cellphones in the Hebert household.

Annette's death had a profound impact on her family, with both Danny and Taylor struggling to cope with her absence. Despite the pain of her loss, Annette's legacy lived on through the precious lessons she taught to those who knew her, as memorialized on her gravestone.]

[The Queen Administrator, also known as the Administrator, is a noble shard that once belonged to the Warrior Entity. Originally used by the Warrior to determine and rearrange the configurations of his shards before distributing them, the Queen Administrator was intentionally crippled and largely destroyed to prevent its host from using it in this fashion during the cycle.

After its crippling, the Queen Administrator specializes in coordinating control over large numbers of smaller lifeforms and generally chooses hosts and triggers that lend themselves to this specialty. Its known hosts include Taylor Hebert, who gained extremely fine control over bugs within a three-block radius; Aiden, who can set rally points to control bird minions; and Danny Hebert, who remained an idle host.

The Queen Administrator is capable of granting a variety of powers related to its specialty, such as Changer/Thinker abilities that allow the host to regurgitate rats as relays for generalized rodent control, or Master/Stranger abilities that enable the host to manipulate the emotions of people and animals within a 3-4 mile range using smaller creatures as vectors.

As the Warrior's counterpart to the Thinker's High Priest shard, the Queen Administrator is a powerful and versatile shard that plays a crucial role in the entities' cycle.]

[The High Priest shard, wielded by the powerful hero Eidolon, is a 'noble' shard according to Glaistig Uaine. As the Thinker's counterpart to the Warrior's Queen Administrator, the High Priest plays a crucial role in leading and manipulating the other shards, or "faerie," as Glaistig Uaine describes them.

Eidolon's shard is responsible for "plotting" and "raising the faerie up as objects for worship," cultivating them to suit the world outside and best manipulate it. This is evident in Eidolon's ability to manifest virtually any three powers he desires, as well as a more 'native' power that allows him to drain the energy of other shards.

The High Priest's true use remains somewhat cryptic, but it is speculated to be responsible for the creation of "superweapons" like the Endbringers in previous cycles or in Eden's vision. Glaistig Uaine also mentions that the High Priest has a "living" counterpart that she refuses to name, further adding to the mystery surrounding this powerful shard.

As one of the most versatile and potent shards, the High Priest represents the epitome of the Thinker's ability to lead and manipulate the other shards, showcasing the immense potential of the entities' powers.]

[The Locker Incident refers to the traumatic event on the first week of January 2011 that culminated in Taylor Hebert's trigger event and subsequent hospitalization. After a long campaign of bullying by Emma Barnes, Sophia Hess, and Madison Clements, the trio filled Taylor's locker with used feminine hygiene products and allowed them to fester over winter break.

On the first day back at school, Taylor was shoved into the locker by Sophia and left trapped inside for over an hour. Overwhelmed by despair and disgust, Taylor triggered with her bug control powers, causing a sensory overload that led to a second, consecutive trigger and a mental breakdown.

Taylor was discovered and taken to the hospital, where she spent a week in the psychiatric ward. Despite Winslow High paying her hospital bills, no witnesses came forward, and the bullying continued upon her return to school a month later.

The Locker Incident not only marked the beginning of Taylor's journey as a parahuman but also served as a stark reminder of the depths of cruelty and isolation she experienced at the hands of her former best friend and her cohorts.]

A high school located in the docks south of the City of Brocktonbay. The school has a lot of gang kids in it, but they don't fight in the school or wear their gang colors. The north side is longer, with an auditorium and more classrooms—a four-story building.  Most of the Brockton Bay Wards team were known to be attending Arcadia High because it's the nicest public school available and a vocational school, allowing the Wards to spend half of their school day working as superheroes. The school has a Faraday cage to block cellphone use.

The Boat Graveyard is an entire section of the coastline where boats have sat for so long that they have either rusted or taken on water. When the industry collapsed in the 90's One container ship was sunken as a form of protest; while the rest were simply abandoned. There are about forty or fifty ships, many larger than skyscrapers.

a location in Brockton Bay, running north-to-south along the beach, east of the Docks.

Boardwalk is one of the main tourist destinations in Brockton Bay. It's considered one of the nicest parts of town and generally considered a safe place to be. Some shops sell dresses for over a thousand dollars, cafes with ludicrously expensive coffees, and stretches of wooden walkways and beaches where tourists can get a great view of the ocean. The Protectorate ENE Headquarters is visible from here.

The Traders on the Boardwalk hire muscle to rough up thieves and chase away panhandlers in order to make it safe for the tourists. The Protectorate HQ is nearby, so criminals have no chance of ever stealing from the Board Walk.

The region of Brockton Bay is located west of the Boardwalk in the north end of the city and the east—the south end of the Docks borders Downtown. It's a party of brockton bay affected by urban decay, with buildings getting worse as you get close to the abandoned beach. It's part of the Brocktonbay compromise of mainly Japanese refugees from Kysuu and other peoples of Asian descent, the area controlled by the ABB. The area had enough warehouses and apartments for even the most destitute to find shelter. It's considered advisable to avoid the area, as the area has a reputation for criminals and gang members. The people living in the Dock are used to paying protection money to the ABB, and it's known as the go-to place if you want sex, drugs, and violence.
The hill rests at the base of the mountains adjacent to Brockton Bay, near the city's western border.

This is the central area of Brocktonbay; it's one of the nicest parts of the city; the streets and sidewalks are wide, and there are skyscrapers in every other lot. The southeast part of downtown was housing. It was relatively nice, although there were some E88 gang tags and broken windows here and there. It was a clashing mix of old and new buildings. Lord Street was the main road that ran through the city and downtown, tracing the line of the bay. The downtown bordered the coast, near the south ferry station. It's a half-hour walk from Winslow High, but it's impossible to catch a bus there and back within the span of an hour.

Somer's Rock is a nondescript pub in the middle of a long street full of hole-in-the-wall businesses. There are iron bars on the windows while the outside paint is peeling, and the rust from the bars has bled onto the gray-white paint below the windows.

The inside of Somer's Rock is "dim, dingy, and depressing." The wood floor is stained the same color as the counter, while the curtains and tablecloths are dark green. The only "real color" or "brightness" is the yellow light cast by old bulbs. It's a family-owned bar with the deaf daughter serving as a server and twin brothers serving as bartenders. The bar is a neutral meeting ground for the villains of Brockton Bay.

Are the under-eighteen sub-division of the Protectorate.  as an initiative to recruit the next generation of heroes.

The concept expanded in the ensuing years and improved with organizations like the Youth Guard forming to help bridge the gap between normal life and duties as a cape. 

Wards are granted a $50,000 trust and a base minimum wage salary, which is doubled on full membership. They are similar to the Protectorate in membership types and status but have additional protections and measures. Probationary Wards lose their status at the age of eighteen, and they cannot access confidential or classified records without permission. Wards must attend school during typical hours and maintain satisfactory grades, with failure to do so resulting in pay docking. They must receive a full night's sleep and are allowed to be removed from school or awakened in moderation.

Transfer of a Protectorate member requires permission from department heads, parents, the Ward, one teacher, or educational voucher. In-house psychiatrists, outside psychiatrists, therapists, and probation oversight must agree. Dissenting parties can contact a higher office to cancel an unwanted transfer and put it on hold for six months.

Termination of a Ward requires a tribunal and thorough review, with punishment or transfer to a better environment preferred over termination. If necessary, measures may include suspension, firing, arrest, and execution. Parental involvement is not required for Wards participating in Cape activities, but parental or guardian consent is required for active membership.

The Wards of Brocktonbay. Aegis is the self-serious leader of the Brockton Bay wards. He's smart and comfortable with his position as leader. A group of Personal assistants and secretaries led by the perfectionist  Supervillian Accord, Located in Boston, Massacutes. The Ambassadors were formed by Accord in order to carry out his long-term plans to benefit humanity. All prospective Ambassadors are accomplished people, or those with the potential to be, that Accord has selected and tested rigorously. At the end of this time, they meet Accord's nigh-impossible standards and are fully on board with his plans. They are almost unbeatable when under Accord's direct leadership. A closely guarded secret in the cape world. They're capes who purchased a vial from the Cauldron and drank it to gain power. A Kill Order is a document issued by the PRT allowing for the murder of a cape with no legal repercussions. A rarely wielded tool, a kill order brings society's wrath down onto its target. Villainous Capes who have broken the unwritten rules and are now deemed a public threat that even other villains agree must be taken out. A bounty using donated public funds is established causing many bounty hunters to seek out the target. Bounty hunters fight over who gets to kill the target and the heroes have to step in to stop the situation from spiraling out of control.  

All members of the Slaughter House 9 have kill orders so do other S-Class threats. Many villains have pre-signed kill orders as a warning to not go too far.

A prison for Parahumans that committed crimes severe enough that they warranted being put inside a prison with no chance of escaping. It's Located inside a hollowed-out mountain in British Columbia, part of the greater Rockies mountain range. The walls are lined with ceramics designed by Dragon; each layer of the mountain contains dormant containment foam, which will automatically start expanding upon a wall breach. Inside the mountain is a vacuum, and three thousand anti-gravity drones will detonate upon detecting an abnormality. Some of them contain containment foam, and some are much more lethal.

The mountain prison is suspended by pipes delivering supplies; it's split into wings with minimal walls, allowing prisoners to intermingle. Cell blocks are organized, with some highly organized, like Marquis' block.

The Manton Effect is a common phenomenon where powers affect living targets or inanimate objects, but not both. It is a result of powers being limited to facilitate human use, with in-built controls to avoid harming parahumans. Most powers have limitations, such as targeting specific materials, range, and precision. This reduces the potential lethality of most powers, such as telekinetics, forcefields, and pyrokinetic, which can cause significant harm.

The PHQ is a floating base of operations that serves as the base of the Brockton Bay Protectorate. It is outfitted with a forcefield bubble and a missile defense system. It is visible from pretty much any point on the Docks, including the Boardwalk. The forcefield made everything seen through it look oversaturated, like a TV with bad picture settings.[3]

The structure was a marvel of architectural design with its arches and spires, lit by tinted spotlights and set on a beautiful platform with hard edges and sweeping lines.

A forcefield roadway is used when traveling to and from the base.

a group of parahumans identified by their typically bizarre or monstrous external appearance. They were so-called because their origin was the 53rd anomalous case investigated by the PRT. All-or-nothing is not strictly linked to the general threat level of a parahuman but denotes the high quality, "hard counter" nature of the power itself they are severely limited in that they have to use their own legs and wits to get to the target, which hurts their general threat levels.: Clockblocker, Eidolon, Gray Boy, and the Siberian are just some examples of All-or-nothing capes.

She enjoys messing with people and being abrasive to gain more information about the target.
