Lisa's enhanced intuition allows her to crack computer passwords, profile people, and make predictions about situations. However, she is not infallible and must consciously direct her power to avoid mental overload and migraines. Tattletale wears a skintight black-and-lavender outfit with black lines, including a stylized "Tt" on her chest, arms, legs, and a stylized eye emblem on her chest. She also wears a black domino mask, conceals freckles, and wears a utility belt with a small gun in one of the larger pouches. She knows that coil is backing the undersiders,because one of his men on the boardwalk caught her using her power to steal clothes from a store.

Alec/Jean-Paul-Vasil(Citizen Identity): He's a Lanky, pretty boy of European descent and black curly hair; he wears expensive, if not particularly attention-grabbing, clothing, preferring to buy new clothes rather than wash something and wear it a second time. He makes a habit of wearing white. He's the son of Heartbreaker, but he hates his father for always trying to control him and never being satisfied with how he kills people. He has no qualms about killing his brothers and sisters if their father sends them after him. He's 15 years old, and he's a gamer. 
Regent(Cape Identity): regent, amoral and bisexual, is a straight-up hedonist driven by pleasure seeking. Regent is perceptive and astute but lacks fitness and commitment. He cares for the Undersiders and is passive-aggressive in conflict. Despite his devil-may-care attitude, he cares for each member of the Undersiders. Regent wears Renaissance-era clothing, leggings, and loose shirts. His Venetian mask features a silver coronet, padded underside, and covers Regent's mouth. Alec is a powerful Master who can cause targeted involuntary movements in others' bodies. He uses this power to trip opponents during battle and finish them off with a taser hidden inside his scepter. His Master 8 rating stems from prolonged use of his ability, allowing him to control all bodily functions and sensory suites. However, Alec's control worsens as the distance between himself and the target widens or when attempting to control more people. This affects his coordination, speech, and fluidity of movement. Alec is highly resistant to the powers of his relatives, such as his father and sister Cherish, who could overpower Alec through concentrated effort.

Brain Laborn(Citizen Identity):Brian, an African-American teenager, is tall, muscular, and handsome, with a deep, masculine voice that could pass for an adult. He has cornrows in his hair. He uses his power to create an echoing effect. He has a unruly little sister named Aisha, who he's trying to gain custody of and, he has divorced parents. His mother is a drug addict and his father is a tough man who doesn't know how to deal with children, especially his little sister Aisha. He's 17 years old.
Grue(Cape Identity): The defacto leader of the undersiders. Grue is professional with a desire for personal freedom and a cautious approach to family and friends. He values practicality and self-discipline, and is proficient in multiple martial arts. He is confident in training his teammates and is open to change. He wears motorcycle leathers and a motorcycle helmet with a full-face visor sculpted to look like a stylized skull. These incorporated side vents to allow the darkness he creates to flow outward, creating an eerie, dramatic effect. Grue generates smoke-like darkness that erases light and mutes sounds, and interferes with microwaves, radio frequencies, radiation, and Breaker powers. His darkness is not visible but does not obscure his vision. Grue's darkness produces a steady air current, making it difficult for those with enhanced senses to track him. It can be moved by strong winds and used to distort his voice and body position. Grue can also form rough shapes and make a body double. His darkness can dissipate at will and selectively.

Rachel Lindt(Bitch): Publically, she's known as a hellhound, but she calls herself Bitch. Her lack of education influences Rachel's complex personality, relationship with dogs, and limited socialization. Her sensitivity to dogs and her remorse for her actions contribute to her skepticism and misunderstandings. Growing up in foster homes with little stability further complicates her personality. She perceives relationships as struggles for dominance and family dynamics. Her personas as Rachel and "Bitch" are closely aligned due to her past as a homeless person pursued by authorities. Additionally, her time on the streets has given her the ability to sleep in stressful environments. Rachel has a squarish face, thick eyebrows, and auburn hair. She is naturally inclined to fitness and uses heavy jackets, boots, and disposable dog masks interchangeably with slight modifications. She is constantly active around her dogs, requiring constant activity to force her dogs around. Rachel's ability to significantly empower dogs to increase size, strength, durability, agility, and an asymmetrical covering is remarkable. This power has impacted her ability to socialize with humans and has given her resilience to certain Master effects. Rachel can use her power at range and on multiple dogs simultaneously but cannot automatically control them. She trains her dogs to respond to whistles and commands, and their dogs gain durability and resistance to pain. However, Rachel must be cautious about feeding too much additional mass to dogs, as they lose agility and other benefits. Her power also affects other canines, such as wolves, which are more effective on wolves than domesticated dogs. Bitch has three dogs trained to obey her under the effects of her power: Brutus, Judas, and Angelica.

Kayden Anders(Citizen Identity): A interior decorator formerly married to Max Anders, the CEO of Medhall. She takes care of her Daughter infant Aster Anders and she pays her step son Theo Anders to baby sit her, she cares about the boy, but she lovers aster more.She has brown hair and eyes, she's shorter than average. Although she claims she isn't racist, her time in the empire made her prejudice against certain people's ethnic backgrounds. 
Purity(Cape Identity): Kaiser's former right hand-woman, he left him after discovering his true character, she still loves the man despite everything.  She can shoot kinetically charged light, moving at high speeds and generating powerful blasts. She can create two curved beams, a double-helix shape capable of leveling buildings, or fire multiple beams simultaneously. Her energy recharges when basked under special halogen lights in Kaiser's office. Sunlight may give her more power than regular light. She's ever since leaving empire 88 with "Night" and "Fog" following suit she's, trying to be a independent hero attacking ABB pimps, gangster and capes three to five times a week. She's tried to cooperate with the authorities she's received nothing but silence in response.

James Fliescher(Citizen Identity): He's the CEO of a pharmacy chain, has a wife and three children, and is friends with Medhall CEO Max Anders. 
Krief(Cape Identity): He's one of Kaiser's Lieutenants in the E88, a part of Gescellshaft, and originally from London. He takes two trips yearly. He lies, saying he's taking a vacation to Brazil or Europe, in civilian life.  Krieg has the power to manipulate kinetic forces in various ways, though it is most powerful within a certain radius of himself. Hostile forces will move slower or be disrupted/deflected by a controlled unconscious air friction/resistance alteration. Hostile enemies may have trouble breathing. In addition, his actions have increased results for the energy involved; he can punt someone to send them flying through the wall, but he's resistant to master effects due to his time in the Geschellshaft. He wears a SS Uniform as his costume.

Dorthy Schmidt(Civilian): Dorothy dresses a little too well, wearing a dress, high heels, lots of makeup, and jewelry. Dorothy has pale blue eyes. She's a charming and helpful lady; She has an unerring morning routine with planned dialogue that she and her husband go through without fail.
Night(Cape Identity): Underneath her guise lies killing intent. The Geschellshaft brainwashed her and her husband. , She wears a black costume with a cowl, mask, hood, high-heeled boots, and a heavy cloak. Her mask exposes her eyes, and she transforms unseen using tools like flash bangs, smoke canisters, and a large, removable cloak with mini-hooks. These tools help her blind her foes and create a net-like effect.
Night, a monster form of Dorothy, is a multi-legged, hyper-agile, lightning-quick death blender with blades and claws. Her amorphous body has sharp edges and long, insect-like legs with claws, making her a multi-legged, hyper-agile, lightning-quick death blender. Her angular legs have no proper joints but can bend and stretch, preventing her from being tripped. Despite being covered in oily lubricant, Night's Breaker state remains underwater, out of sight, raising questions about the duration of her alternate state. Her monstrous form has immense strength and speed, capable of incapacitating any of Bitch's dogs and shattering their protective bone plating. Night can achieve high speeds, make sharp turns, and navigate obstacles easily, making her appear to be teleporting. she's left the empire (for now) along side her husband and purity.

Geoff Schmidt(Civilian Identity): He's married to Dorthy Schmidt. Like his wife, he always dresses a little too well for situations wearing a shirt, slicked-back hair, and a blazer. He has an unerring morning routine with planned dialogue that he and his wife go through without fail, a result of their brainwashing by Gesellschaft. To an observer, he and his wife are boring; the most interesting thing is that they own a cat.
Fog(Cape Identity): He wears a gray costume with a hood and mask, largely a gray masculine version of his wife's costume without her other equipment. Like hers, it lacks accouterments or other paraphernalia being draped over him. Geoff transforms into a living fog, causing harm to those within. He can shift his body into a gaseous entity with varying solidity. If inhaled, Schmidt can erode living matter in his radius and cause internal damage. His gas can cause permanent lung damage to those within it, counteracting healing factors. He's left the empire(for now) alongside his wife and purity.

A cruel and manipulative man with a love of theatrics. Jacob had a playful demeanor even while committing small-scale personal pain or coordinating wide-scale atrocities with the backing of the Slaughterhouse Nine. Every move and action he made was calculated to afflict change in the world around him for the worse. He expresses a love for affecting "keystones" in his viewpoint chapter that could change the world around themselves as well as though he was an individual butterfly effect which highlights his grandiose self-perception. At his core, Jack is a shallow person. He is not genuinely charismatic and an edge lord; his power is doing all the work. Jacob, tall and slender, wears civilian clothing and has a face similar to Johnny Depp's, pale blue eyes, a full beard, a severe widow's peak, and a mustache trimmed in goatee fashion. He's showing signs of aging, having a few white hairs and minor wrinkles around his eyes.  Jacob's ability extends the cutting edge of any handheld-edged weapon beyond its physical dimensions, providing infinite range. He uses an imaginary projection that does not damage the blade while in use, allowing him to augment the strength of cuts, thrusts, slashes, and stabs. However, his capabilities are limited by the blade's physical capabilities. Jacob's power is not limited to knives; he finds them faster and easier to handle. The Manton Effect treats Hookwolf's metal parts as inorganic, allowing Jacob to affect shapeshifted Hookwolf blades. Bonesaw modified members of the Nine with protective safeguards, wire reinforcement, and artificial neurons, rendering them resistant to pathogens and allowing them to make plans. Jack has a secondary power so subtle he doesn't even notice it; Unconsciously alerting Jack to potential attacks from hostile parahumans, his administration may nudge them to dissuade them. If isolated, the Nine's passengers may nudge their hosts toward the hostile parahuman's location. The hostile parahuman's passenger may liberally interpret existing drawbacks to favor Jack.

Riley Grace Davis (Bonesaw), Riley is a young girl who loved her family, in 2005 the Slaughter House 9 invaded her family's home and tortured her family over and over again until Riley was triggered trying to save her mother; this led to drastic changes in her personality, with becoming Bonesaw a childish and carefree character who enjoys murder and torture. She is fixated on being a "good girl" and avoiding swearing. Bonesaw craves love from the Nine, who she considers her "family." She has nightmares about her trigger event and dreams about sleeping without being held by one of her older teammates, usually the Siberian. Bonesaw seeks to please Jack Slash, her mentor, teaching her to view her torture methods as art. She relentlessly pursues innovation in her art, seeking inspiration and new ways to make others suffer. When in a bad mood, she is one of the most dangerous of the Nine. A young girl in a dress with blond hair curled in ringlets. She has one blue eye and one green eye. Over her dress, she wears a stained, oversized apron with a pocket that carries her vials and surgical tools. Aside from her hair, which is kept immaculate, her body and clothes are unkempt, covered in dirt and blood. She is almost always accompanied by her biomechanical "spiders," small metal boxes with needles and scalpels at the end of their hydraulic legs. She's terrible at naming her creations.  Bonesaw is a formidable Tinker with expertise in biological, anatomical, and physiological sciences. She performs various surgical procedures to enhance her allies' and victims' bodies, making her one of the most dangerous Tinkers on Earth Bet. Her status is due to her extensive research and the materials used. Bonesaw can alter the Corona Pollentia, allowing her to modify parahuman abilities to a limited extent. She can fuse multiple coronas to create powerful powers, such as Cherish's ability to sense negative emotions and combine two parahumans by horribly meshing them together to make one terrifying and powerful cape. Bonesaw can effectively collaborate with and incorporate technology from other tinkers, possibly due to her enhanced connection with her shard. However, she finds working with non-biotech technologies frustrating and slower.

Cherish(Cherie Vasil) is the wayward daughter of Heartbreaker, the eldest sister of Regent. She's intelligent and lacks emotional capacity, almost to the point of being a sociopath. She was raised in an environment of hedonism and exploitation; she could indulge in any vice she desired from a young age. Unlike her brother, she revels in exploiting and using her abilities. Wanting to forge her path, she descended into becoming a serial killer and joining the Slaughter House 9. Cherie is a slim, conventionally attractive young woman with dark hair and a red streak. During the Slaughterhouse Nine's tests, Mannequin had tattoos on her stomach and chest with gigantic, hideous raised tattoos that distorted her body and distracted her from her natural beauty. When Jack Slash could think of nothing more to be done during his test, he had her go through the other tests again, leading her to get a matching tattoo across her back. Cherish possesses the unique ability to detect and control emotions, perceiving them as distinct "sounds" associated with different feelings. This allows her to track individuals across a city and understand their relationships. She can also induce emotions in others and build a dependency by repeatedly influencing their emotions. She gained a group of followers through this method. Additionally, her powers facilitated language acquisition due to her intuitive understanding of meaning. Cherish's powers were resistant to similar Master-class abilities, and she could interfere with other Masters. Her powers were ineffective against certain individuals with unique resistances, such as Regent, Gallant, and Glory Girl. Despite limitations, her powers were effective against certain Stranger-type infiltrators like Satyr but not against Imp, although she can sense Imp's emotions.

The Siberian is the most powerful member of the Slaughterhouse Nine and one of the most powerful capes on the planet. On September 15th, 2000, Siberian fought Hero, Alexandria, Eidolon, Legend, eight other Protectorate capes, and the PRT. They attacked her while she was pinned down. During this battle, she tore Hero and destroyed one of Alexandria's eyes before mysteriously escaping and joining the slaughterhouse 9. She continues attacking the protectorate; she lays low with the slaughterhouse9 between their slaughters. Her favorite member of the slaughterhouse 9 is bonesaw, seeing her as a daughter.  She doesn't speak often; most people think she's incapable of speaking. The Siberian is a black and white striped woman with glowing yellow eyes and unknown nationality. Her hair is waist-length and sharp, turning her nails into deadly weapons. She is often covered in gore and slicks off windows. The Siberian is both an unstoppable force and an immovable object. The Siberian is an unstoppable force that can easily navigate through obstacles and people. She is immune to physical forces and attacks, and can sway her hair in the breeze. She can bestow invulnerability on anyone or anything she is in physical contact with, allowing her to make huge leaps on unstable surfaces. She can grant invulnerability to up to five individuals at once. Although she cannot fly, she has the physical power to move quickly, ignoring air resistance and minimizing inertia. Skitter compared her leaps to an arrow loosed from a bow, and she can travel faster than Bitch's dogs, Crawler and Shatterbird.

Crawler is a masochist who seeks extreme danger to expand his abilities and join the Slaughterhouse Nine.He enjoys taunting and torturing his victims, causing fear among the public. Crawler desires to be hurt and has been used against him in various situations, such as being persuaded to stand under Bakuda-bombs for injury. Taunts can provoke him to attack despite apparent traps. Crawler is a six-legged beast with a black body, armor plates, scales, spines, and bristling hair. He has a hundred solid-black eyes and six legs, each forking at the knee or elbow joint. His rear limbs have claws and tentacles, while his forelimbs have claws and long-fingered hands. Crawler is verbally communicative but has a low, resonant grumble. Taunts can provoke him to attack despite seeing a trap. Crawler's power lies in permanent adaptive regeneration, which allows him to heal injuries at incredible speeds. His core, located in his brain, is the weak point of his regeneration, and he can regenerate hundreds of pounds of flesh in a few heartbeats. Crawler's adaptation is the primary focus of his power, and he gains mutations for every X points of resistance he takes. This allows him to develop both defensive and offensive adaptations over time.Crawler's armor can withstand a small nuke and walk unscathed through burning buildings. His internal organs have been rearranged and reinforced with numerous redundancies, and he has hundreds of eyes set into his armor and an enhanced sense of smell for tracking. His modular limbs ensure his dexterity hasn't suffered for his growth, and he has an incredibly strong caustic spit that can launch at targets.Crawlers can only adapt when regenerating from resistible damage, and they cannot adapt to All-or-Nothing attacks or psychological effects.He cannot adapt to psychological powers.

Shatterbird was born in the United Arab Emirates and was unknowingly dosed with a Cauldron formula, prompting the manifestation of her powers and the deaths of thousands. She eventually made her way to London, then America, joining the Slaughterhouse Nine. She thinks of herself as a scholar and recruiter directly recruiting burnscars during one of her sprees. She's known for her control-freak nature and pride. She enjoys city-wide attacks and the psychological effects they have on her victims and their loved ones. She harbors romantic feelings towards Jack but never acts on them and justifies herself with excuses. Shatterbird hates Cherish for nominating herself to the Nine. Shatterbird, a Middle Eastern-looking silica kinetic, wears a helmet, flowing garment, and a beaked glass mask. She controls the glass, sand, and other siliceous compounds within her location. She can create projectile weapons, target storms, fashion makeshift shields, and fly by controlling the glass in her costume. Her range for these fine-tuned abilities is longer than Cherish's offensive range. Shatterbird can hear sand, detect people digging, and has a flying speed lower than Siberian and Crawler's. Her power is subject to the Manton Effect and cannot affect plants. Bonesaw-modified members of the Nine with protective safeguards, including sheathing vital organs and major arteries, wire reinforcement, and artificial neurons.

Burnscar's mental state is influenced by her power, which she uses to control her recklessness and guilt. She tests potential members of the Nine by forcing them to face their greatest fear. Mimi, a pyrokinetic who can teleport herself through flames, is a versatile character with a psychopathic nature. She can create concussive fire blasts, shoot twin flamethrower-like streams, and send fire "snaking" across the water. Her power adjusts chemical balances and connections in her brain, reducing empathy, impulse control, and emotion. Mimi's eyes glow and occasionally flash orange when active. Bonesaw-modified members of the Nine with protective safeguards, including sub-dermal mesh, wire reinforcement, and artificial neurons. She also rendered her teammates resistant to her pathogens and granted them artificial neurons, allowing them to make plans Cherish could not see. She's friends with Shatterbird; they get along well with each other. She desires to visit Brocktonbay to visit her friend Elle; she doesn't want her to join the slaughter house nine she just wants to talk to her and reminisce about their days in the Parahuman asylum.

Armsmasters is the leader of the brockton bay protectorate and one of the top heroes in the world, being featured in photoshoots with the core group of the protectorate. Armsmasters is a stern and uncompromising man. He sees himself as a soldier of law and order fighting against supervillains. He is known for his tunnel vision and self-reliance, pushing himself to his limits. Armsmasters' pride allows him to take on any job and perform any role the Protectorate requires; he doesn't have a single infraction on his record. He deliberately went without family, friends, or personal life to improve his life as a cape. Colin's pride and anger can lead to errors in judgment, narcissism, and difficulties in understanding people. He is tall, dark brown, and wears a dark-brown beard. His costume comprises midnight-blue power armor, a helmet, and a visor. He wields his Halberd weapon system, a lie detector, and a computer program to predict enemy behavior. He also uses a personalized tinker-tech motorcycle. His chest emblem features a silhouette of his visor in blue against a silver background and is featured on various merchandise, including underwear. Colin is a Tinker focusing on miniaturization, efficiency, and hybrid technology. He creates efficient technological devices, including blades that can cut through steel, grappling hooks, welding devices, flails, and teleportation. His equipment includes temporal stasis triggers, EMP projectors, plasma blades, echolocation, Lie detectors, combat predictors, psychic shielding, sealed biohazard capabilities, enhanced strength, megaprojects, and nano-thorn disintegration fields. Armsmaster secretly resents Dauntless.

Hana, a parahuman who survived a 1985 Kurdish village attack by Turkish soldiers, was rescued by an American and brought to the United States. She was fostered and placed in the Inaugural Wards Team, and her name was anglicized from Hana to Hannah. She formed lasting friendships with many of her teammates and had a short relationship with Chevalier. After working under Alexandria and the Triumvirate, she was in Brockton Bay under Armsmaster. Hannah is a steady, rational person who believes her power has taken the angriest parts of her, including her dreams and forgotten parts, and given them concrete form in her power. She follows the law's letter and is the Protectorate's natural leader. Hannah's power is a green and black, semi-sentient blur of energy that can form into ordinary-looking weapons. She can re-summon a weapon at will, making it easier to use nonlethal ammunition. Her power influences her ability to use the weapons, enhancing her draw time and aim and subtly adjusting their balance. She can accurately shoot a target's head and neck, re-summon her weapon from someone's hands, and shoot the wielder before they react. Known options for her power include a sheathed combat knife, Bowie knife, cutlass, steel machete, pistol, Beretta 92 FS, handgun with silencer, rifle, sniper rifle, assault rifle, two assault rifles, machine gun, Uzis, shotgun, hollow-point bullets, rubber bullets, smoke grenades, rocket launcher, flamethrower, grenade launcher, mortar, harpoon gun, and ten-foot-long bomb, possibly nuclear. She doesn't need to sleep, making her a Noctis cape.

Shawn(Citizen Identity): Shawn and Kelly lived in a mobile home with a child, Addison, who had schizophrenia. They had a happy relationship. In 1996  they were trapped in a mudslide. Shawn performed a C-section on Kelly to save Addison's life and triggered. After Kelly left, Shawn married Jennifer, who was ambitious and financially responsible. He realized they were mismatched and separated from her. 
Dauntless(Cape Identity): A powerful figure in Brockton Bay, he was initially unaware of his power until he realized it worked. He became a rising star in April 2011, and his abilities became widely known, making him a popular hometown hero. Dauntless can empower items by infusing them with a small amount of power each day, permanently enhancing them. He wields a spear, shield, and boots, all enhanced with this ability. It is believed that Dauntless would eventually equal or surpass the Triumvirate, but no one is certain if his power would eventually level off. Dauntless is constantly "charged" with energy, which builds up over time and can be used to dump excess charge into an object. He charges the same object regularly and focuses on three or four cycles between them. Objects gain general durability and physics immunity and gain other abilities after the 20th charge. It takes around a month for Dauntless to develop a new power to impact a confrontation. Dauntless's items include an arclance, a spear made of white lightning, a shield of a metal disc surrounded by rings of the same energy, and boots that allow him to fly. He wears gold and white armor, rumored to have been enhanced with his power. Dauntless also wears a gold Greek-style helmet, granting him sensory and protective abilities.

Ethan was a jailbreak specialist known as Madcap; he committed over a hundred felonies in six years, breaking out numerous people en route to the incarcerated in the birdcage. He battled Battery eight times before she eventually defeated him, leading to his arrest. After being caught, he joined the Protectorate as "Assault" and was required to be on the same team as Battery. As a hero, he continually pestered Battery for a date. Armsmaster struggled to deal with his harassment of her.Eventually, she agreed in exchange for forcing him to help her with community outreach, which she mistakenly assumed he would hate. Eventually, he and Battery married, though this was unknown to the public; some speculate that he might be her brother.. Ethan is smart, witty, and observant; he can catch Battery's trepidation about discussing her powers. As Assault, he wears red body armor and is a kinetic energy manipulator. He can move over long distances at speeds similar to Chariot, cross rooms with a single leap, and resist incoming containment foam. Ethan's flexible power allows him to hit armored vans, rip doors off armored vans, and smash weapons against the ground. His power is ineffective when in midair.

Jamie(Citizen Identity): Battery is the daughter of a detective who was tired of seeing the work put into apprehending villains put to waste by Madcap. Cauldron contacted her while shopping for tinker-made equipment and agreed to a meeting to discuss buying powers from them. She then worked out a deal for superpowers she couldn't afford in exchange for doing a total of three favors. She eventually defeated Madcap; he joined the protectorate as a probationary cape and renamed himself to assault as a way to mess with Battery.  After much pestering, she started Assault dating and eventually married him. 
Battery(Cape Identity): serious and willing to work hard. She feels guilty about the deal she made with Cauldron. This guilt carries over to her career as a hero, where she goes above and beyond the call of duty. The battery is 5'3.  She wears a skintight white and dark grey costume with circuit-like cobalt blue lines, which glow as she charges her power in an electric blue-white color. Battery can charge up her power and release it to boost her speed, strength, and electromagnetic powers. She is almost invincible while charged, faster and stronger than Assault, but requires concentration and staying still. She can run at a speed of 7-12 seconds, dodge streams of containment foam quickly, and can throw objects like a frisbee. She can also use her remaining charge to move metal objects, pour energy into an item, and even deflect a blade fired by Mannequin. However, her power is not conventionally Manton-limited.

Rory Christner(Citizen Identity): The son of the mayor of Brockton Bay, Roy Christner. He has two little sisters, who are twins. Rory was a perpetual second-place baseball player until he went to his father for help. His father gave him a vial that enhanced his strength, speed, and capabilities. Unfortunately, it destroyed his dreams of playing Major League baseball months later. The Leagues started mandating MRI scans for all players to "check for powers and maintain the integrity of the game. He joined the Brockton Bay Wards in 2008 after his dreams of being a baseball player were destroyed. 
Triumph(Cape Identity): His time in the wards has given him a strong sense of right and wrong. He's dating Prism, a cape in the New York Protectorate. As Triumph, Rory has a gladiator/lion theme to his costume, with a gold lion helm, shoulder pads and belt, and skintight suit. Rory's main power is sound manipulation - he can control its force, area of effect, and unleash it in bursts. He also sports a mild healing factor, healing quicker than average with minimal scarring. Triumph also has some level of super-strength, being able to punch through concrete. As of April 8th, 2011, he's graduated from the wards into the protectorate.

Robin Swoyer (Civilian Identity): Robin enlisted in the military due to the promise of a way to learn languages (Russian and Chinese) and hoped to travel during/after the fact. Instead, he got stuck in the rank and file with no follow-through and longer terms than expected. He eventually triggered after being "caught in a bad situation in a bad place and mental state. Robin joined the Protectorate. He also has started taking some classes in Chinese on the local Protectorate's team to give them an edge while dealing with the Azn Bad Boys. As Velocity, Robin wears a red costume with racing stripes down either side and two stripes meeting in a 'v' on his chest. His costume didn't include a "cup", allowing increased mobility.
Velocity (Cape Identity): Robin likes being a cape and is happy to have an 'out' from military service, which could have killed him well due to his despair and frustration if nothing else. However, he still feels quite frustrated. His ambition was to learn languages and travel. Robin can change states by altering the way time or physics work in relation to himself, resulting in a breaker state that allows him to function without breaking bones, friction, or running out of oxygen. However, it also prevents him from lifting small objects and makes his punches weaker than an eight-year-old at high speeds. His power reduces the effect of melee attacks, but it doesn't make him immune to poison. Velocity's perceptions and body are accelerated, making him impossible to hit in melee. He is fast enough to run on water and outrun vehicles and is the only Brockton Bay Protectorate member capable of keeping up with Purity and Dauntless. However, Grue's darkness interferes with his power, affecting his ability to feel his way to targets and strike at them with around half effectiveness. He is fast enough to prevent insects from landing on him and kill those that do, but he becomes vulnerable if distracted and unable to dodge attacks he can't see coming.

Sophia Hess(Citizen Identity): Sophia is an 15 year old african american teenage girl attending Winslow High. She's slender and has long, straight hair. She's a mean-spirited teenager and track and field team member. She has disdain for those she perceives as weak and hates anyone she can't beat in a fight. Understandably people at her school don't like her, but she's best friends with Emma Barnes and Madison Clements, so people have to deal with her. Sophia's bullying tends toward physical violence, such as tripping, punching, kicking, and shoving. Her favorite person to bully is Taylor Hebert, Emma Barnes's former best friend. Sophia has a single mother who works two jobs to support herself, her older brother Terry, and a younger sister who's four years old. Sophia doesn't help around the house.
Shadow Stalker(Cape Identity): Sophia, a powerful and mysterious character, wears a heavy black cloak and a skintight black bodysuit with black-painted metal kneepads, gauntlets, belts, and pockets. Her mask takes the shape of a woman's face, leaving her brown eyes visible behind it. Sophia is described as wispy and transparent, nearly invisible, and has a distorted, skull-like face hidden by her mask. She can shift into a "shadow state" that allows her to pass through walls and make her lightweight. She is vulnerable to electricity and has lenses built into her mask to detect electricity. Sophia's power can phase a weapon into a target and bypass armor, leaving a characteristic imprint on the victim. Her power negatively interacts with Grue's darkness, making it difficult to breathe in her shadow state and forcing her into a middle ground where she is slower and painful to re-form after objects pass through her. She was recruited when she was arrested for almost killing a man by crucifying him with her crossbow bolts; she agreed to join the wards under the condition she would be a probationary ward, and the PRT covered up her attempted murder. The public likes her, but her fellow doesn't like her; the feeling is mutual.

Carlos: Carlos Is a seventeen-year-old man of Puerto Rican descent who wears long hair. He triggered at the age of fifteen. 
Aegis(Citizen Identity): He's the newest leader of the wards, taking triumph place shortly after he graduated into the protectorate. He wears a rust-red costume with a matching helmet, silver-white trim, and a shield emblem. His costume leaves some of his skin exposed and his eyes visible. He carries a variety of grenades (flashbang, tear gas, incendiary, etc). Aegis is a flying, augmented physiologist with a unique biology that allows him to sense light with his skin when his blinded, bleeds out an excess amount of blood and survives decapitation. His augmented physiology allows him to abuse his body, resulting in supernatural strength. He can throw punches that break his hand, mangle joints, and tear muscles and experience adrenaline rushes to keep going. Aegis does not feel pain, but his powers allow him to deal with drawbacks. It remains unclear if Aegis has congenital insensitivity to pain or if he handles the sensation. With his adaptive brute ability, Aegis is capable of defeating Glory Girl.

Dennis: Dennis is Caucasian with red hair, blue eyes, and about average height. He attends Arcadia High in Brocktonbay.  Dennis triggered when he was 15. While donating bone marrow to his father to help with his condition, the stress of the situation gave him his powers. The needle that was about to be inserted into his bones when extracting marrow was what shaped his powers into a striker ability, being able to pause time as his father's was rapidly running out.  
Clockblocker (Cape Identity): Dennis, a hero, is known for his humor and wit, possibly due to his father's life-threatening illness. Clockblocker, a hero, is willing to work with villains but never crosses the line and joins the dark side. He wears a skintight white costume with glossy white armoring covering every inch of his skin. The armor has grey clocks inscribed on it, and his hands move at different speeds using digital displays. Clockblocker's helmet is a faceless, smooth expanse of white.
Clockblocker cannot disable the effects of his power, which causes objects to remain frozen for 30 seconds to 10 minutes without control over the time limit. His powers are comparatively static throughout the storyline, working through interconnected objects but with a limited range.

Missy Bryon: Missy Byron is 12 years old; she was born on 15th May 1998. She triggered in 2009, joining the Wards a month shy of eleven years old. Her trigger event was caused due to her parents' hostile relationship with one another. Her father had cancer, and her mother cheated on him with his brother. Her father then got back at her mother by getting rid of her dogs. This enmity grew over time. They divorced, causing her to withdraw into her position as a Ward and identity as Vista. She had a scar on her chest where she was stabbed by Hookwolf and sewed it up herself rather than risk looking like a baby in front of her team.
Vista: She's the youngest and most experienced member of the Brockton Bay Wards,she has a crush on Gallant, and everyone can tell. Vista, a strong-willed and focused Shaker, can distort non-living material and manipulate terrain. She wears a costume with wavy lines, body armor, and a green visor. Her powers involve warping spacetime, causing projectiles to be redirected, but her reflexes are too slow to deflect projectiles. Her mental map of the terrain is provided by solid matter, and she can target specific objects, which remain small and lightweight until her power wears off. She is classified as a Shaker 9, especially compared to other Shakers in Brockton Bay. However, her powers can confuse some thinkers' powers and computers. Vista can anchor her space-warping effects on projections and tools, increasing their size or manipulating the space that matters creation and energy occupies, which may be difficult for parahumans to work around. Her power synergizes well with Clockblockers.

Chris(Citizen Identity): Chris fifteen-year-old boy attending Arcadia High. He was diagnosed with ADD and dyscalculia before he gained his powers. Although he resisted the ADD diagnosis, he couldn't deny the dyscalculia. He became even more distractible after gaining his power. Eventually, he joined the Brockton Bay Wards and gained access to far more materials. Chris has brown hair and a pale complexion.
Kid Win: He wears red and gold body armor with a red visor. As a Tinker, Chris can understand and invent things well beyond the current level of technology. He hasn't figured out his specialty yet.  Kid Win uses a hoverboard for flying and a Spark Pistol for non-lethal sparks. He created Gallant's power armor but didn't maintain it. Kid Win has a giant Alterator Cannon but hasn't been approved by the PRT Military or the science team. Other weapons include large power armor, Tac radar, and a transformer handgun with non-lethal rounds.

Bruce (Cape Identity): He's a handsome and pretty intelligent guy. He progressed through high school and craved solitude even while his social circle thwarted this desire. This, combined with insomnia and general indifference, eventually took him to a psychologist, after studying his family history, came to the tentative conclusion that he might have schizophrenia, yet to manifest. While out with a friend's family on a boat, He decided to see what would happen if he threw himself into the freezing waters of the bay, he had physical trauma and almost drowned, and he triggered. The PRT discovers his power after a fast recovery, and the family and PRT discuss options to balance mental health and powers. For now, Browbeat stays with the Wards, testing his abilities and taking on various heroes. The PRT recruits Browbeat, recognizing his reputation as a troublemaker, and recruits him to gain the necessary training and skills for his future.
Browbeat: His cape identity is rather baseline; with his powers, he can achieve a muscular physique that dwarfs many bodybuilders and borders on the absurd. His costume was a dark blue spandex piece with a diamond print; his full-face mask only left his eyes uncovered and was topped with a crystal on the forehead. His costume does not include body armor. He's new to the Brocktonbay Wards.  Browbeat's biokinesis enhances his physical strength, allowing him to patch wounds, harden tissues, and accumulate calcium. He can also reshape his features, qualifying him for a Changer rating. As he gains familiarity with his powers, he can dampen burn damage by creating heat-resistant chemicals, neutralizing toxins, and increasing insulation and conductivity. Browbeat can modify his appearance marginally, unable to affect fine detail changes. Interestingly, he avoids conflict, a trait he shares with his parents.

Dean Stansfield(Citizen Identity): Dean has blond hair,[ broad shoulders, and a narrow waist. He's 17 years old and a little taller than Victoria Dallon. He's in line to be the heir of his parents' company. They were rich enough to buy him superpowers. While going to Arcadia High, Dean met and, later, started dating Victoria Dallon. Dean was nearby when she triggered and gained her powers. Since his passenger was stubborn enough to maintain the broadcast signal, Victoria's aura is influenced by his powers despite being disconnected. His family kept horses. He's taken Victoria Horseback riding a few times. He comes across as a natural gentleman, which may have been influenced by his ability to see people's emotions in a way no one could hide. He lives in the towers.
Gallant(Cape Identity): In costume, he pretends to be a tinker in public by wearing 'secondhand' power armor made by Kid Win and Maintained by Armamaster. He hopes to be able to help Amy with her emotional state. Dean, an empath, could generate concussive energy blasts that could alter emotions and pack a punch. He was versatile in his energy use, able to lob cannonball-sized orbs or shoot them from his fingertips in tight beams. He could inflict specific emotions on his opponents, but the effect is unreliable when used on individuals like Hellhound, who are not neurotypical. Dean also could sense the emotions of those around him but struggled to distinguish between them. As an emotion manipulator, Dean would be resistant to and interfere with other emotion manipulators, confusing Cherish's emotional topology and harming her with his concussive blasts. He could target those affected by Cherish's emotional manipulation, either dismissing the effect or leaving people debilitated.

Victoria Dallon, also known as the Glory Girl, is a hot-tempered, prideful seventeen years old teenage cape, the daughter of Brandish and Flashbang of New Wave. Victoria is a tall, platinum-blonde young woman. As Glory Girl, she wears a white one-piece dress that ends in a skirt at her mid-thigh with shorts underneath, an over-the-shoulder cape, high boots, and a golden tiara with spikes radiating from it. She enjoys fighting and is protective of her family, especially her adopted sister Amy. She likes to give the impression that she's invulnerable. As a kid of known superheroes, Victoria was welcomed into the elite student circle, which led to her growing disillusionment with life. Before gaining power, Victoria wanted to be a superhero, leading her to play sports and start dating a hero. In 2009, at 14, Victoria triggered when she was fouled in a basketball game, causing her to fly. Around a year later, she was attacked by a gang called the Chorus. Amy triggered her, healing her. It was publicly known that Victoria is dating Dean Stansfield, and it's an open secret among the heroes that Dean was the secret identity of the hero Gallant. She's a Classic Alexandria package; Victoria possesses flight, invincibility, and superhuman strength. She radiates an aura that makes her allies respect her and intimidate her enemies. Victoria's invisible forcefield extends over her skin and clothes, which requires a recharge after a heavy impact or sustained fire. Her forcefield protects her clothing and Glory Girl costume, but the skirt is inconsistently protected. Victoria can also radiate energy that makes anyone in her presence feel an emotional charge of awe, admiration, or raw intimidation. This power is considered a Shaker ability, not a Master's power, and she gained it by triggering in Gallant's vicinity, making it difficult for him and other emotion-based parahumans to read or influence her.

Amy Dallon is Victoria's adoptive sister, a talented biokinetic with healing power. She can modify the biology of living organisms but strictly avoids altering brains. Panacea experiences guilt and resentment for not helping others, leading her to resent her patients. She held a strong code of behavior and power, refusing to kill or interfere with human minds. Breaking these guiding tenets caused mental stress. Amy's thinking is backward and toxic, with a tendency to start from the endpoint and work backward. She is stubborn and resistant, often deciding to take what she needs if she believes someone is a Villain. Amy's adoptive mother, Carol Dallon, is cold and suspicious of her due to being the daughter of her rival, Marquis, and her adoptive father, Mark Dallon, is too depressed to show her affection. Her sister, Victoria Dallon, consistently showed her affection and was strongly attracted to Victoria. She keeps this secret, fearing it will ruin their relationship, but she's extremely jealous of her boyfriend, Gallant. Amy is terrified of combat and avoids it entirely. Amy has frizzy brown curly hair and freckles from forehead to chin, packed densely enough that there were as many brown freckles as pink skin. As Panacea, Amy wears a robe with a large hood and a scarf that covers the lower half of her face. The robe is alabaster white and has a medic’s red cross on the chest and the back.Amy is a biokinetic with the ability to modify the biology of any living organism she touches, including humans and all carbon-based life. She primarily uses her power for healing and has the ability to render parts of a person's body numb. However, her power is slow and requires an appropriate supply of material to perform changes. Amy cannot work directly with dead tissue, such as hair or fur, and corpses. She is capable of modifying brains but has a firm rule against it, fearing what may happen if she crosses this line. Amy's changes are deep and not easily corrected compared to other master effects. Additionally, any attempt at neural diagnostics puts her into a state of partial shared consciousness.
